wheat/insect.1.name: Aphids
wheat/insect.1.symptom: Insects present clustered on the leaves; as the infestation progresses the numbers increase and they secrete honeydew on which the black sooty mould fungus grows.
wheat/insect.1.appearance: During January and February; the infestation intensifies during March.
wheat/insect.1.timing: When infestations of aphids appear in any numbers.
wheat/insect.1.guidance: Do not delay the planting date, given the spread of other hosts from which the pest moves to wheat flies.

wheat/fungus.2.name: Loose smut in wheat
wheat/fungus.2.symptom: Appears on all parts of the spike except the rachis and turns them into a black powdery mass of dark fungal spores. The infected spikes usually emerge a few days before the healthy ones. The infection is spread by wind, which carries the fungal spores that attack healthy spikes at the flowering stage. The rachis of the infected spikes appears completely bare of any spikelets at the end of the season.
wheat/fungus.2.appearance: At heading, as the infected spikes emerge early.

wheat/fungus.3.name: Powdery mildew in wheat
wheat/fungus.3.symptom: The infection appears on the leaves as pale greyish-white spots, after which the characteristic powdery appearance of this disease forms on the upper surface of the leaves, then moves to the lower surface as the infection progresses. When the infection becomes severe, small black bodies appear, which are the fruiting bodies of the fungus.
wheat/fungus.3.timing: At the start of the appearance of the infection.

wheat/fungus.4.name: Yellow (stripe) rust
wheat/fungus.4.symptom: Pustules appear slightly raised above the leaf surface, yellow in colour, circular in shape, arranged in longitudinal rows parallel to the leaf axis, hence it is called stripe rust. The pustules appear on all parts of the plant (leaves - stems - leaf sheaths - spikes). When the infected leaf is wiped by hand, it leaves traces in the form of a yellow powder.
wheat/fungus.4.appearance: When suitable environmental conditions are available, at the beginning of the second half of February the disease symptoms begin to appear on susceptible varieties, and the disease develops and unfolds during March and April.

wheat/fungus.5.name: Fusarium diseases in wheat
wheat/fungus.5.symptom: It is one of the secondary diseases that have been recorded in some types of soils outside the valley (reclaimed lands) or in lands that suffer to some extent from drought. The symptoms appear as a brown discolouration in the root system and the crown region, turning black when the infection becomes severe. Infection of seedlings leads to their death, and infection of the adult plant causes the spikes to dry before grain set is complete.
wheat/fungus.5.appearance: This disease appears at the seedling stage and the adult plant stage.

wheat/fungus.6.name: Root rot and damping-off
wheat/fungus.6.symptom: It infects the seeds before the seedling emerges above the soil surface, whereby the radicle of the plant embryo is infected with rot as soon as it emerges from the seed, and in this case the seedlings do not appear above the soil surface. Seedlings above the soil surface are infected, as the fungus attacks the seedlings at or slightly below soil level, causing rotting of the stem so that it cannot support the parts above it.
wheat/fungus.6.appearance: The fungus causes the death of plants before they appear above the soil surface, or they die as soon as they appear above the soil surface.

fieldbean/insect.1.name: Aphids
fieldbean/insect.1.symptom: Insects present clustered on the growing tips of the plants; as the infestation progresses and the insect numbers increase, they secrete honeydew on which the black sooty mould fungus grows, so the terminal leaves of the plants turn black.
fieldbean/insect.1.appearance: One week after the seedlings emerge above the ground
fieldbean/insect.1.timing: When infestations of aphids appear in any numbers.
fieldbean/insect.1.guidance: The importance of detecting aphid infestation in its early stages and dealing with it as foci - since aphids transmit viral diseases that severely affect faba bean productivity - so it is important to scout regularly after the seedlings emerge above the ground and to treat the initial infestation foci with one of the recommended specialised pesticides.

fieldbean/mite.2.name: Red spider mite
fieldbean/mite.2.symptom: Spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe, spider webs form on the lower surface; the leaves and buds fall off when the infestation is severe as a result of feeding on the plant sap.
fieldbean/mite.2.appearance: From the emergence of the seedlings until harvest.
fieldbean/mite.2.timing: At the seedling stage when 3-4 individuals are present per plant, or when the infestation is detected at the flowering stage.

fieldbean/fungus.3.name: Brown spot
fieldbean/fungus.3.symptom: Reddish-brown spots of various shapes and sizes on the lower leaves, then the edge of the spot becomes darker than its centre, and the infection extends to the leaf petioles and the stem in the form of elongated spots.
fieldbean/fungus.3.appearance: The month of December, and it intensifies during January and February
fieldbean/fungus.3.guidance: Be cautious with irrigation during February and March to limit the infection, while taking care to reduce the pressure of the spray solution at flowering.

onion/insect.1.name: Thrips
onion/insect.1.symptom: Yellowing of the plants in cases of severe infestation, with silvery spots appearing on the leaf blades; these spots draw closer together in cases of severe infestation, as the spots turn grey and then brown and then dry out - yellow and orange nymphs are seen in the heart of the plant, as well as dark-coloured winged individuals.
onion/insect.1.timing: When the numbers reach 10 nymphs and adult insects per seedling of the seedlings examined at random.
onion/insect.1.guidance: Treatment can begin one month after planting, with the spraying repeated 15 days after the first spray when necessary.

onion/fungus.2.name: Downy mildew
onion/fungus.2.symptom: Oval or elongated cylindrical spots of various sizes, pale green in colour - the black fungal spores appear on the surface of the spots - the flower stalks cannot support the inflorescences and become twisted, taking the shape of a goose's neck in the red onion grown for seed production.
onion/fungus.2.appearance: All stages of plant growth, depending on the environmental conditions prevailing in the different cultivation areas.

onion/fungus.3.name: White rot
onion/fungus.3.symptom: Infected plants occur as scattered patches in the field, and the symptoms appear as yellowing, then wilting and death of the leaves from the tip of the leaf downward and from the old outer leaves to the young inner leaves. Rots appear on the roots below the soil surface, and when the infected plants are uprooted, a white cottony growth is seen on the infected bulbs, and small black sclerotia the size of a pinhead form on them.
onion/fungus.3.appearance: The symptoms of infection begin to appear in late December and early January and continue until late February and early March, after which the disease stops due to the rise in temperature, which is unsuitable for the occurrence and development of the disease.
onion/fungus.3.timing: Dipping the transplants before planting in fungicidal disinfectants, with spraying with these disinfectants 6 and 12 weeks after planting, or according to the pesticide's own recommendation.

onion/fungus.4.name: Purple blotch
onion/fungus.4.symptom: The infection appears on the leaves and flower stalks as oval or round spots that take the form of sunken lesions with concentric rings, with a purple or blackish centre and a pale yellow margin; the infected tissues dry out and turn crimson, then brown.
onion/fungus.4.appearance: This disease appears in late February and early March, and it often appears accompanied by downy mildew.
onion/fungus.4.timing: Spraying 45 - 60 days after planting, or at the start of the infection, or when suitable environmental conditions are present.

onion/fungus.5.name: Pink root disease
onion/fungus.5.symptom: It appears as a pink or crimson colouring of the roots of the infected plants, which then dry out and die; the plant continues to form new roots that are also infected, and this leads to yellowing and stunting of the plants and a small size of the resulting bulbs, exhausting the food in forming roots, and they are unmarketable.
onion/fungus.5.appearance: At any time in the plant's life, especially in the case of drought, high heat and poor soil.
onion/fungus.5.timing: Treatment of the transplants before planting.

garlic/insect.1.name: Thrips
garlic/insect.1.symptom: Silvery spots appear on the leaf as a result of the insect feeding on the plant sap; the adult insects appear in black and the nymphs in yellow, and the critical maximum ranges from 10 - 15 insects per plant.
garlic/insect.1.appearance: From the month of October until the end of the season, but its numbers begin to increase gradually from late January until the crop matures.

garlic/mite.2.name: Garlic bulb-drying mite
garlic/mite.2.symptom: Presence of spots and streaks on the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe, curling and death of the leaves occur
garlic/mite.2.timing: As soon as the symptoms of infestation appear.

garlic/fungus.3.name: Downy mildew
garlic/fungus.3.symptom: The symptoms begin to appear in January, as grey spores grow on the surface of the old (aged) leaves, and the leaves become pale green then turn yellow and die; the infected area varies according to the severity of the infection, and the spread of the disease varies according to the direction and speed of the wind. The disease spreads quickly in the presence of wind and when fog, dew and rain are available, and the infection increases on cold nights followed by a warm day.
garlic/fungus.3.appearance: All stages of plant growth, depending on the environmental conditions prevailing in the different cultivation areas.

garlic/fungus.4.name: Rust disease in garlic
garlic/fungus.4.symptom: The infection appears on the leaves and petioles in the form of pustules; the pustules are reddish-brown in colour and are the uredinial spores of the fungus. At the end of the season the pustules turn blackish-brown as a result of the formation of the fungus's teliospores, and the leaves turn yellow and dry out, which affects the formation and size of the heads and makes them small, and therefore leads to a lower yield; these pustules may appear on the garlic heads in cases of severe infection.
garlic/fungus.4.appearance: This disease appears in some areas where rainfall is abundant and which are characterised by high humidity; the epidemiology of the disease varies from one year to another.

sugarbeet/insect.1.name: Beet tortoise beetle
sugarbeet/insect.1.symptom: The adult insects and their various larval stages make holes in the leaf surface resembling shot holes, and when the infestation becomes severe the leaf becomes torn and tattered.
sugarbeet/insect.1.appearance: The infestation begins to appear from the beginning of March
sugarbeet/insect.1.timing: When the average number of larvae of various ages reaches 15 larvae per 100 plants of the plants examined at random.
sugarbeet/insect.1.guidance: The infestation appears early in lands that do not follow a proper crop rotation, and it also intensifies in late plantings. Care should be taken to cover the foliage with the spray solution.

sugarbeet/insect.2.name: Cotton leafworm
sugarbeet/insect.2.symptom: The small larvae may begin feeding on the cotyledons and attack the true leaves, the buds and the stems of the tender seedlings, which leads to the death of some plants in the infested hills or the loss of plants in them at this early stage of growth.
sugarbeet/insect.2.appearance: The cotton leafworm infestation intensifies on the plants of the two early seasons (August and September), which results in the death of seedlings one month after planting, and this requires replanting the damaged hills with transplants, especially beet plantings adjacent to cotton fields.
sugarbeet/insect.2.timing: When the average number of egg masses reaches 10 egg masses per 100 plants of the plants examined at random.
sugarbeet/insect.2.guidance: Treat only the infested foci, taking care to spray on the newly hatched larvae.

sugarbeet/insect.3.name: Leafminers
sugarbeet/insect.3.symptom: The infestation causes winding silvery mines on the leaves, and increased severity of infestation leads to the collapse of the leaves and their failure to carry out photosynthesis.
sugarbeet/insect.3.appearance: From the end of February until the month of March.
sugarbeet/insect.3.timing: When an infestation rate of 3 - 5 % in the leaves examined at random is reached.

sugarbeet/insect.4.name: Beet leaf miner fly
sugarbeet/insect.4.symptom: The infestation by the beet leaf miner fly appears as interlaced mines in the form of pale-coloured patches resulting from damage to large areas of the green leaf tissues.
sugarbeet/insect.4.appearance: The infestation by the beet leaf miner fly appears in the period from (November - April), and the eggs are laid in groups, often on the lower surface of the leaves.
sugarbeet/insect.4.timing: When the infestation in the leaves reaches 40 infested leaves per 100 plants of the plants examined at random.

sugarbeet/fungus.5.name: Leaf spot
sugarbeet/fungus.5.symptom: The symptoms of infection with the disease appear as circular spots with a well-defined edge on the old leaves, 2 - 5 cm in diameter; these spots are brown in colour with a purple edge, and they also form on the leaf petioles as elongated spots. As the infection progresses, these spots spread more and merge with each other and cover a large part of the leaf surface, and may cause the leaf to dry out and die, remaining attached to the crown region, whereas the heart leaves are usually free of infection.
sugarbeet/fungus.5.appearance: Suitable conditions from the month of December until the month of February, in association with the age of the plant (three to four months) - and these suitable conditions for the appearance of the disease coincide with the early seasons (the months of August, September and October).
sugarbeet/fungus.5.guidance: Planting resistant varieties while obtaining healthy seed from reliable sources, and collecting the residues of the previous crop and destroying them by burning, as the causal agent survives in them; following a suitable crop rotation, in which beet is not planted repeatedly in the same land, is also beneficial.

sugarbeet/nematode.6.name: Root-knot nematode
sugarbeet/nematode.6.symptom: Appearance of nematode galls on the roots and tubers accompanied by yellowing of the leaves and wilting and stunting of the plants.
sugarbeet/nematode.6.appearance: One month after planting, and it intensifies during the growing season
sugarbeet/nematode.6.guidance: The pesticide is applied as a spray or broadcast (depending on the form of the preparation) onto the soil immediately before irrigation.

alfalfa/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
alfalfa/insect.1.symptom: Larvae feeding on the foliage, making holes and causing damage to the crop used as livestock fodder - and the presence of large larval stages and pupae in the soil under the plants.
alfalfa/insect.1.appearance: With the planting of berseem clover, especially early planting in October, and in cases of severe infestation the matter leads to replanting.
alfalfa/insect.1.timing: When the infestation appears in newly germinated berseem clover and 5% infestation is present.
alfalfa/insect.1.guidance: The preparation is sprayed on the newly hatched larvae.

cotton/insect.1.name: Mole cricket
cotton/insect.1.symptom: Wilting of plants while they are still attached to the soil, which makes them easy to pull out; also the presence of winding feeding tunnels slightly raised above the soil surface (1 - 1.5 cm in diameter), especially in the bottom of the furrow and heading toward the hill, and the infestation increases in fields fertilised with farmyard manure or close to villages.
cotton/insect.1.appearance: It can begin from the placing of the seed.
cotton/insect.1.guidance: The pesticide is used as a poison bait, prepared as follows: 15 kg of cracked maize or local bran + 20 L of water + the recommended pesticide; then the land is irrigated in the morning, then the poison bait is scattered between the rows at sunset.

cotton/insect.2.name: Whitefly
cotton/insect.2.symptom: Curling and downward bending of the leaf margins - observation of the adult stages of the insect.
cotton/insect.2.appearance: From mid-March to mid-May - and from the first half of July to the end of the season.
cotton/insect.2.timing: When the infestation reaches 7-10 insects per plant of the plants examined at random. And when hanging yellow traps, when the count is 50 insects (cumulative number).
cotton/insect.2.guidance: Spraying is carried out on the foliage.

cotton/insect.3.name: Aphids
cotton/insect.3.symptom: Curling and downward bending of the leaf margins. Secretion of honeydew to which dust sticks. As the infestation becomes severe, the colour of the leaves changes to black, and sooty mould grows on them.
cotton/insect.3.appearance: From the end of March to the end of May and from mid-June to mid-August, and it begins at the edges of the field facing cucumber or adjacent to other crops.
cotton/insect.3.timing: When the infestation is first detected at the field edges or as foci inside the fields, and the infested foci and the plants surrounding them are treated.
cotton/insect.3.guidance: In the case of seed treatment, the seeds are moistened with water, then mixed well with the pesticide and left to dry, then planted immediately, or they are mixed mechanically with the seeds.

cotton/insect.4.name: Cotton leafworm (newly hatched larvae)
cotton/insect.4.symptom: Presence of moving larvae - feeding marks on the leaves - smell of the hatching; also the first and second instars may scrape the lower epidermis of the leaves.
cotton/insect.4.appearance: The last week of May and the beginning of June, then the infestation by the first generation on cotton continues, depending on the planting date and the weather conditions.
cotton/insect.4.timing: At the start of the appearance of newly hatched larvae clustered at the egg-mass site.
cotton/insect.4.guidance: Bio-pesticides are sprayed when newly hatched larvae appear, and for the other pesticides spraying is done when the colour of the egg masses turns grey.

cotton/insect.5.name: Cotton leafworm
cotton/insect.5.symptom: Presence of moving larvae - feeding marks on the leaves - smell of the hatching; also the first and second instars may scrape the lower epidermis of the leaves, while the third instar makes holes less than 1 cm in diameter, and the fourth instar makes holes larger than 1 cm, whereas the fifth and sixth instars eat most or all of the leaves.
cotton/insect.5.appearance: The last week of May and the beginning of June, and the infestation intensifies during June, and this represents the first generation on cotton.
cotton/insect.5.timing: When the number of moths caught in water traps reaches a rate of 50 moths over three full days.
cotton/insect.5.guidance: Spraying is carried out on the foliage when newly hatched larvae appear in the case of bio-pesticides, and when egg masses appear in the case of conventional pesticides.

cotton/insect.6.name: Bollworms
cotton/insect.6.symptom: In the case of recent infestation of the bolls by the pink bollworm, it is difficult to identify the infested boll from its external appearance - the presence of holes in the bolls indicates the exit of pink bollworms, and spiny bollworms may also make an exit hole, or an entry hole into another boll, or one for pupation; its hole is distinguished by its jagged edges and is coloured by the larva's excrement.
cotton/insect.6.appearance: From the first of July, the assessment of the appearance of bollworm infestations on the formed bolls begins.
cotton/insect.6.timing: Spraying is carried out on the same day on which the infestation rate in the examined bolls reaches 3%, taken at random from the examination unit (feddan) of 30 bolls, or when 8 moths are caught in 3 consecutive nights using paper traps starting from the first of July. Spraying is carried out immediately in the case of infestations by recent larval instars "small sizes", and in the case of infestations by advanced larval instars "large sizes" spraying may be delayed until a week after the infestation is assessed.
cotton/insect.6.guidance: Organophosphorus pesticides can be mixed with one of the moulting inhibitors when the appearance and presence of the cotton leafworm coincide with the first spray against bollworms with organophosphorus pesticides, and spraying is done on the foliage.

cotton/mite.7.name: Red spider mite
cotton/mite.7.symptom: Pale white spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves, starting around the midrib of the leaf and extending outward. This is followed by the appearance of a reddish-purple colour on the lower surface of the leaves.
cotton/mite.7.appearance: Mid-March to mid-May and until the end of the season.
cotton/mite.7.timing: It can begin at the seedling stage when 3-4 individuals are present per plant, and at the vegetative growth and flowering stage when an average of 4 individuals per leaf is present among all the leaves examined at random.
cotton/mite.7.guidance: Treatment is carried out by fan-pattern spraying to ensure that the pesticide reaches and covers both the upper and lower leaf surfaces.

cotton/fungus.8.name: Root rot and damping-off
cotton/fungus.8.symptom: Absence of hills as a result of the seeds not germinating, and when the hill is dug up the germinated seeds appear in a state of rotting. Seedlings may appear above the soil surface leaning, with a brown lesion on them bearing fungal growth (the symptom of sudden collapse), and seedlings may die without collapsing (the symptom of seedling blight), and plants can tolerate the infection with a brown lesion on one side of the stem near the soil surface when the temperature rises.
cotton/fungus.8.appearance: From the planting date until 4 weeks of age after germination, and the symptoms may continue to appear on the upper roots until two months of age.
cotton/fungus.8.guidance: Seeds are treated with pesticides before planting, especially when planting early in cold weather in lands adjacent to rice plantings.

roselle/fungus.1.name: Powdery mildew
roselle/fungus.1.symptom: A white powdery growth appears on both surfaces of the leaf, and the petals and stems of the plants are infected with the same symptoms - the infection occurs first on the leaves at the crown region, on the lower surface, then yellow spots appear on the upper surface of the leaf; as the infection develops the adjacent spots merge until the powdery growth of the fungus covers the entire leaf surface in grey. Large plants are infected first and the infected leaves usually die.
roselle/fungus.1.appearance: When suitable conditions of warm temperature and moderate humidity are available.
roselle/fungus.1.timing: At the start of the appearance of the disease symptoms.

rice/insect.1.name: Bloodworms (in transplanted rice)
rice/insect.1.symptom: The larvae feed on small rice seedlings, which causes these seedlings to gather above the water surface in the corners of the basin, leaving their place as patches free of plants.
rice/insect.1.appearance: The beginning of May on small rice seedlings. In fields irrigated with drainage water or water mixed with it.
rice/insect.1.timing: When the infestation appears, especially in nurseries irrigated with drainage water or in places of high salinity.
rice/insect.1.guidance: Spraying or scattering of granules is done one day after sowing the nursery, and water is not drained from it for a week, while compensating for the water lost.

rice/fungus.2.name: Blast
rice/fungus.2.symptom: The infection appears on the leaves in the form of small spindle-shaped spots (3 cm long × 1 cm wide), bluish-brown in colour, and when the spots enlarge their centre becomes grey and their edge dark brown - the infection appears on the stem (the spike stalk) in the form of dark or light grey spots causing neck blast, and the infection may extend to the grain husks, which become pale white in colour.
rice/fungus.2.appearance: All stages of plant growth from the nursery until heading
rice/fungus.2.timing: As soon as the infection appears.

rice/fungus.3.name: False smut
rice/fungus.3.symptom: The symptoms appear on individual grains (3-4 grains per spike) and usually on a small number of spikes depending on the severity of the infection. The typical appearance of the infection is in the form of a spore ball (about 1 cm in diameter), initially orange-yellow in colour, turning over time to dark olive. This spore ball encloses the individual grain, as the growths of the causal fungus take the place of the internal tissue components of the grain. This spore ball is a source of infection in the same season for adjacent spikes or in the following season through seed contaminated with it.

rice/fungus.4.name: Foot rot and elongation (Bakanae)
rice/fungus.4.symptom: Various symptoms of the disease appear, the most important being elongation in the growth of seedlings in the nursery or the permanent field, and also death of seedlings in the case of severe infection, accompanied by yellowing of the plants and reduced tillering. These symptoms become distinctive of the disease at first sight, as the plants appear as if foreign to the variety. With advancing age some of the infected plants die. And in case the plant continues to grow, it may not produce any spikes, or it produces weak spikes with unfilled grains, which affects the yield, and the seed of infected fields becomes a source of infection in the following season.
rice/fungus.4.appearance: The symptoms begin to appear in the nursery 15 - 25 days after sowing the seed.

rice/nematode.5.name: White tip nematode disease
rice/nematode.5.symptom: The symptoms appear on the leaves in the form of curling of the leaf tips with white to grey discolouration, and also clearly on the flag leaf; the length of this curling varies according to the severity of the infection and also the variety. Stunting appears on severely infected plants, and the spikes are stunted and empty or have a high proportion of empty grains, and the spikes may not emerge completely.
rice/nematode.5.appearance: The symptoms appear on the leaves about 45 - 60 days after planting.
rice/nematode.5.timing: At the time of sowing the nursery.

sorghum/insect.1.name: Cutworm
sorghum/insect.1.symptom:
- Attacks maize seedlings in their early growth stages
- Complete cutting of the stem of small seedlings at soil level or slightly above, causing the affected plants to wilt, then die and fall to the ground separated from the roots
- When searching beneath the affected plants, brown larvae curled in the shape of the letter C are seen
sorghum/insect.1.appearance: In the early growth stages of the seedlings.
sorghum/insect.1.guidance:
- Take care of agricultural operations such as ploughing, hoeing and weed removal.
- Do not overuse organic fertilization.
- Use light traps.

sorghum/insect.2.name: Cotton leafworm
sorghum/insect.2.symptom: Presence of egg masses on the leaf blades. Presence of larvae of various ages on the plants. Presence of feeding marks on the leaves. Presence of larval frass in the leaf axils.
sorghum/insect.2.timing: When 10% of plants are infested with an average of one larva per infested plant.
sorghum/insect.2.guidance: Maize adjacent to vegetable and clover fields is severely infested in the months of August and September.

sorghum/insect.3.name: Fall armyworm
sorghum/insect.3.symptom: Young larvae feed on the leaf tissues from one side and make irregular holes in the leaves; in severe infestation the growing tip may die early in the season, which is called the dead heart phenomenon.
sorghum/insect.3.appearance: From the emergence of seedlings until the appearance of the ears.
sorghum/insect.3.timing: When moths appear in the pheromone traps (see Annex Three).

sorghum/insect.4.name: Corn borers
sorghum/insect.4.symptom: Presence of egg masses on the lower surface of the leaves - presence of larval entry holes on the stem - bending of the male inflorescence due to a partial break in it.
sorghum/insect.4.timing: When egg masses reach 25 egg masses / 100 plants on the lower surface of leaves examined at random.
sorghum/insect.4.guidance: To protect the plants from infestation, the planting date recommended by the Ministry (approximately 15 May - 15 June) must be observed. The spray solution must also cover both surfaces of the plant leaves completely.

sorghum/fungus.5.name: Root rot and damping-off
sorghum/fungus.5.symptom: The fungus kills young seedlings before or just as they emerge from the soil, attacking the growing tips of the seedling; before dying they may show brown discoloration and decomposed water-soaked areas. The main symptom is an increase in the proportion of missing hills due to seedling death. Brown spots appear on the roots of the plants, and these spots weaken the seedling stem in the affected area, causing it to fall and die, and it is easily uprooted.

sugarcane/insect.1.name: Soft scale insect
sugarcane/insect.1.symptom: The insect is found on the lower surface of the leaves, and as the infestation increases, stages of the insect are found on the upper surface, where they feed by sucking the sap, leading to the appearance of honeydew on which the black sooty mould fungus grows, with accumulation of dust.
sugarcane/insect.1.appearance: Starting from July, with the peak of infestation in mid-August and after.

sugarcane/insect.2.name: Greater sugarcane borer
sugarcane/insect.2.symptom: Holes and eating of leaves, wilting of plants in the early stages, and ease of pulling out the heart as a result of the infestation.
sugarcane/insect.2.appearance: With the start of seedling emergence in April.
sugarcane/insect.2.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.

sugarcane/fungus.3.name: Whip smut
sugarcane/fungus.3.symptom: The affected plants elongate and are thin with long internodes, and the number of tillers at the roots increases and takes on a grass-like appearance, as the leaves are thin, upright and have narrow blades. The affected ratoons and buds begin to grow faster than healthy ones, and thus the affected plants grow faster than healthy ones. Among the most important distinctive symptoms of this disease is the elongation of the growing tip of the affected plant and its swelling (as a result of a hormonal disorder in the affected plants) in the form of a long cylindrical body resembling a whip (the kurbaj); it is unbranched but twists around itself to form something like a spiral, and it is the growing tip of the plant or the inflorescence which the disease has destroyed and in place of which it has formed a black powder of its spores. The colour of the whip develops from silvery to slate-coloured, then to grey, and finally turns charred black, and in the end the whip bursts so that the black spores spread onto neighbouring plants and into the soil, and the air around the infection is also contaminated.
sugarcane/fungus.3.appearance: The primary infection begins to appear 3 - 4 months after planting, with symptoms appearing on plants of new plantings and on ratoons.
sugarcane/fungus.3.timing:
1. Treating the seed-cane cuttings with the pesticide before planting.
2. When the disease begins to appear in the field or in neighbouring fields.

sugarcane/fungus.4.name: Root rot in sugarcane
sugarcane/fungus.4.symptom: Appearance of lesions in the form of water-soaked spots, reddish-brown in colour and surrounded by a brown margin, on the roots and the embryonic radicle; in severe infection these spots widen and become black with a rough texture. The infection leads to small, weak plants with little branching, and yellowing and curling of the leaves, especially when irrigation intervals are far apart, and the disease may kill the roots, especially in heavy soils, and the whole plant may finally die. When infected plants are removed from the soil, a small number of root hairs formed is noticed, and the root system dies in case of severe infection.
sugarcane/fungus.4.appearance: At any stage of plant growth.

groundnut/mite.1.name: Red spider mite
groundnut/mite.1.symptom: Red spider mites are present on the lower surface of the leaves, where they feed by sucking the plant sap, leading to the appearance of small round yellow spots, so the leaves look bronze-coloured; when the infestation intensifies the leaves turn brown, and the mites can be seen with the naked eye moving on the lower surface of the leaf.
groundnut/mite.1.appearance: The groundnut crop is exposed to severe infestation by the red spider mite, in both its green and red forms, during the different growth stages, from the seedling stage until harvest.
groundnut/mite.1.timing: When 5 motile individuals are present on the lower surface of the compound leaf.

groundnut/fungus.2.name: Root rot and damping-off
groundnut/fungus.2.symptom: Missing hills - death of seedlings before or after their emergence above the soil surface as a result of root rots.
groundnut/fungus.2.guidance: When soaking the seeds, take care to use chlorine-free water such as canal water or artesian well water. If tap water is used, collect it the night before and leave the water in a wide container (basin) to ensure the chlorine evaporates. In all cases, take care to use clean containers during use.

groundnut/fungus.3.name: Leaf spot
groundnut/fungus.3.symptom: Brown spots on the leaves surrounded by a yellow halo, which merge together when the infestation intensifies, leading to drying of the leaves and their falling.
groundnut/fungus.3.appearance: After two months from planting, depending on the relative humidity level.

groundnut/fungus.4.name: Fruit (pod) rots
groundnut/fungus.4.symptom: The apparent disease symptoms differ according to the type of causal agent, and the appearance of the affected pods ranges from rot or brown lesions, or pink rot, or may take the form of complete collapse of the fruit as a result of the severity of the rots.
groundnut/fungus.4.appearance: It begins to appear in the field at harvest and the infection develops in storage and during transport and shipping, especially when poorly ventilated conditions are present in stores or in containers and ships during shipping and transport for export abroad.
groundnut/fungus.4.timing: Treat the infested soil, 50 days after planting, with one of the recommended fungicides.

groundnut/nematode.5.name: Root-knot nematode
groundnut/nematode.5.symptom: The symptoms of nematode infection appear in groundnut fields as patches scattered across the field, with yellowing of the leaves resembling nutrient deficiency symptoms and stunting of the affected plants; when severely affected plants are uprooted, nematode galls or swellings (Galls) are noticed on the roots as well as on the pods, leading to their deformation or a decline in their economic value, and (these galls differ from bacterial nodules in that they cannot be separated easily like bacterial nodules, which form on one side of the roots, and the bacterial nodules also appear red inside).
groundnut/nematode.5.appearance: The symptoms of infection begin in all growth stages of groundnut plants, whether in the seedling stage, the vegetative growth stage, or the stage of flower and pod formation.
groundnut/nematode.5.timing: Treating the infested soil, before planting, with the recommended nematicide.

sesame/fungus.1.name: Charcoal rot
sesame/fungus.1.symptom: It appears as a blackish-brown discoloration of the stem where it meets the soil, and the infection extends up the stem towards the branches and down towards the roots; the plants wilt and die. Among the distinctive signs is the colouring of the plant with a sooty black colour as a result of the fungus forming sclerotia, which can be seen when the bark is peeled off.
sesame/fungus.1.appearance: Symptoms appear late in the season during the flowering and fruiting stage, especially under conditions of drought and high temperature.

sesame/fungus.2.name: Root rot and damping-off
sesame/fungus.2.symptom: Damping-off symptoms appear as rotting of the seeds beneath the soil surface, where the symptoms appear as missing hills, in what is known as pre-emergence damping-off; seedlings may also be infected after germination, and the symptoms appear as sunken lesions on the roots, and the roots are infected with brown lesions that turn black.
sesame/fungus.2.appearance: Symptoms appear at any time of the season, from planting and throughout the growing season, especially under conditions of high humidity.

sunflower/fungus.1.name: Powdery mildew
sunflower/fungus.1.symptom: The symptoms appear on the upper surface as white spots with a powdery appearance, corresponding on the lower surface to yellow spots, and as the infection progresses they take on a blackish-brown colour, and near harvest the powdery growth covers all leaf surfaces, leading to the falling of the leaves.
sunflower/fungus.1.appearance: When suitable conditions of warm temperature and moderate humidity are available.
sunflower/fungus.1.timing: When the disease symptoms begin to appear.

sunflower/fungus.2.name: Root rot and damping-off
sunflower/fungus.2.symptom: Damping-off symptoms appear as rotting of the seeds beneath the soil surface, where the symptoms appear as missing hills, in what is known as pre-emergence damping-off; seedlings may also be infected after germination, and the symptoms appear as sunken lesions on the roots, and the roots are infected with brown lesions that turn black.
sunflower/fungus.2.appearance: Symptoms appear at any time of the season, from planting and throughout the growing season, especially under conditions of high humidity.

soybean/mite.1.name: Red spider mite
soybean/mite.1.symptom: Appearance of pale yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves around the midrib, extending outward and then turning brown; when the infestation intensifies the leaves wilt and die.
soybean/mite.1.timing: When 5 individuals per leaf are present, as an average, in leaves examined at random.
soybean/mite.1.guidance: Spray when the infestation appears and repeat the spraying when needed; the spraying should be uniform with coverage of the lower surface of the leaves.

tomato/insect.1.name: Cutworm
tomato/insect.1.symptom: The infestation is severe in the winter season and in spring - complete cutting of the plant stems at soil level appears - the affected plants also die, especially in the seedling stage. Curled larvae are seen beneath the affected plants, and the infestation is usually in patches of the field.
tomato/insect.1.appearance: During the seedling stage until the stems become woody.
tomato/insect.1.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.
tomato/insect.1.guidance: The pesticide is used as a poisoned bait, prepared as follows: 25 kg of cracked maize or local bran + 20 L of water + the pesticide at the recommended rate. The poisoned bait is placed in small handfuls beside the hills at sunset.

tomato/insect.2.name: Whitefly
tomato/insect.2.symptom: The direct damage consists of curling, yellowing and wilting of the leaves and general weakness when the infestation is severe - appearance of honeydew when the population increases - appearance of symptoms of the viral disease TYLC between 20-30 days after transplanting the seedlings into the permanent land, depending on temperatures, represented by curling and rolling of the leaves, their yellowing, stunting and deformation of the plants, fewer flowers and fruit set, small fruit size and failure of the fruits to ripen, and a sharp decrease in yield.
tomato/insect.2.appearance: From May until the end of November in nurseries and fields.
tomato/insect.2.timing: Adult insects must be completely prevented from infesting the nurseries. Control of the insect in the fields must continue, especially after transplanting the seedlings and for at least 45 days, in order to control the spread of the tomato yellow leaf curl virus.
tomato/insect.2.guidance: Spraying is done on the foliage.

tomato/insect.3.name: Aphids
tomato/insect.3.symptom: Individuals of the pest of various ages spread on the lower surface of the leaves and feed by sucking the sap, and when the infestation intensifies honeydew appears on which the black sooty mould fungus grows.
tomato/insect.3.appearance: From the end of March until May and during August and September.
tomato/insect.3.timing: When the infestation reaches 1-2 individuals/plant on plants examined at random.
tomato/insect.3.guidance: The infested spots of the field are treated. The plants are covered completely with the spray solution.

tomato/insect.4.name: Tuta absoluta
tomato/insect.4.symptom: The larvae feed, making mines in the leaves and in the fruits, causing their damage, and the larvae pupate in the soil.
tomato/insect.4.appearance: In the summer season starting from April and in the Nile season starting from September.
tomato/insect.4.timing: When the number of mines reaches 2-3 mines per leaf.
tomato/insect.4.guidance: Spraying is done on the foliage.

tomato/insect.5.name: Cotton leafworm
tomato/insect.5.symptom: Feeding appears on the epidermis of the lower surface of the leaves in circular areas, by the newly hatched larvae - in the case of infestation by large larvae they eat the leaves directly and make holes, and sometimes feed on the fruits and growing tips.
tomato/insect.5.appearance: Throughout the year in nurseries and in the permanent land.
tomato/insect.5.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.
tomato/insect.5.guidance: Treatment is carried out after irrigation, once the soil can bear walking on it. The plants are covered completely with the spray solution.

tomato/insect.6.name: American bollworm
tomato/insect.6.symptom:
- The larvae damage the reproductive organs of the plants such as buds and flowers.
- The infestation on the fruits is distinguished by the presence of circular-shaped hole openings.
- The larva prefers green, unripe tomato fruits and feeds at the junction of the stalk with the fruit, where the front of the larva's body appears inside the fruit and the rear of the body outside it, with droppings at the opening of the tunnel entrance, which leads to rotting and damage of the fruits.
tomato/insect.6.appearance: At the beginning of fruit set and the beginning of the appearance of the infestation.
tomato/insect.6.guidance:
- Agricultural sanitation and getting rid of the weeds that the pest infests
- Collecting infested green fruits and destroying them with the larvae in them
- Using pheromone traps for male moths of the American bollworm (tomato fruit worm)

tomato/insect.7.name: Tomato fruit worms
tomato/insect.7.symptom: Damage to fruits and holes as a result of larval feeding.
tomato/insect.7.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.

tomato/insect.8.name: Leafminers (genus Liriomyza)
tomato/insect.8.symptom: The larvae feed between the two epidermal layers of the leaf, forming thin, winding mines that gradually widen and at their ends form patches free of tissue, transparent in colour, turning brown as a result of the death of the epidermal cells.
tomato/insect.8.timing: When the number of mines reaches 3-2 mines per leaf of the leaves examined at random.
tomato/insect.8.guidance: Spraying is carried out on the foliage.

tomato/mite.9.name: Red spider mite
tomato/mite.9.symptom: The red spider mites feed on the lower surface of the leaves, so that bronze-coloured spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves, which widen and merge, and the leaf turns brown as a result of the death of the leaf cells; the infestation is distinguished from below by the presence of spider webs on which the mites move. When the infestation becomes severe, symptoms appear on the fruits.
tomato/mite.9.timing: When the average number of mites reaches 7 individuals per leaf of the leaves examined at random.
tomato/mite.9.guidance: The plants are sprayed, covering the lower surface of the leaves.

tomato/fungus.10.name: Fruit rots
tomato/fungus.10.symptom: Hard, sunken spots form, whose colour varies according to the causal pathogen, in the areas where the fruits touch the soil or are exposed to high humidity.
tomato/fungus.10.appearance: The symptoms appear when weather conditions of moderate temperature and high humidity are available, from the month of September.
tomato/fungus.10.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

tomato/fungus.11.name: Root rot and damping-off
tomato/fungus.11.symptom: It is caused by numerous fungi and results in the absence of hills (planting spots) in the early period of the plant's life, before germination or after their emergence above the soil surface, leading to a shortage of standing plants in the field.
tomato/fungus.11.appearance: At the beginning of the plant's life and at any stage of growth.
tomato/fungus.11.timing: Treatment of the seeds or seedlings before planting.

tomato/fungus.12.name: Powdery mildew
tomato/fungus.12.symptom: Bright yellow spots appear on the upper surfaces of the leaves, corresponding on the lower surface to fine, delicate growths of white or light grey colour; as the infection becomes severe these spots turn brown and dry out.
tomato/fungus.12.appearance: After two months from planting and according to the planting season (crop cycle).
tomato/fungus.12.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.
tomato/fungus.12.guidance: The spray solution must reach the upper and lower surfaces of the leaves.

tomato/fungus.13.name: Early blight
tomato/fungus.13.symptom: Spots on the surface of the lower leaves extending to the upper leaves, characterised by concentric rings around their centre, and cankers on the stem and spots on the fruits, especially at the stalk end, also characterised by concentric rings around their centre. They are of a blackish-brown to black colour.
tomato/fungus.13.appearance: The infection appears on the leaves, stems and fruits during periods of moderate temperature and high humidity.
tomato/fungus.13.timing: When the infection appears, especially in the summer season.

tomato/fungus.14.name: Late blight
tomato/fungus.14.symptom: Large, irregular, water-soaked, dark greenish spots form on the stems, leaves and fruits; as these spots enlarge their colour turns dark brown, and in humid weather a grey downy growth forms on the lower surface of the leaves surrounding these spots.
tomato/fungus.14.appearance: The disease spreads in high humidity and low temperature.
tomato/fungus.14.timing: When the infection appears, especially in the Nile season.

tomato/fungus.15.name: Soil diseases
tomato/fungus.15.symptom: Symptoms appear on the seeds in the nursery in the form of seed rot under the soil surface, where the symptoms appear as an absence of roots, or the seedlings may be infected after germination and the symptoms appear as sunken cankers on the roots; severely infected seedlings often die, and the roots are infected with brown cankers that turn black.
tomato/fungus.15.appearance: At the beginning of the plant's life and at any stage of its growth.
tomato/fungus.15.timing: Treatment of the seeds or seedlings before planting.

tomato/nematode.16.name: Root-knot nematode
tomato/nematode.16.symptom: Galls appear on the roots, followed by yellowing of the leaves, wilting and stunting of the plants, and deterioration of the yield.
tomato/nematode.16.appearance: From the small seedling stage to the fruiting plant.
tomato/nematode.16.timing: Detecting any population in the soil at the start of the season is considered dangerous and treatment must begin immediately.

potato/insect.1.name: Cutworm
potato/insect.1.symptom: The larvae gnaw the small seedlings at soil-surface level, either completely, so that the seedling dies, or partially, so that it leans and wilts, with small crumbled green pieces appearing that the worm gnawed but did not eat. The infestation appears in foci and does not cover the whole field.
potato/insect.1.appearance: During the seedling stage and before the stem becomes woody.
potato/insect.1.guidance: The pesticide is used as a poison bait, prepared as follows: 25 kg of fine bran + 20 L of water + the recommended pesticide. The land is irrigated in the morning, then the poison bait is scattered between the rows at sunset.

potato/insect.2.name: Mole cricket
potato/insect.2.symptom: The insect feeds on the seed tubers and the roots of small plants. Signs of infestation also include holes and cavities in the potato tubers, which reduces their marketing value, and in the stems and branches in the lower areas next to the soil surface the plant leans; when the infestation becomes severe the plant dies, and lumps consisting of the remains of the insect's feeding together with its droppings appear on the soil surface. Wilting and death of small plants is observed as a result of the insect cutting the seedling above the soil surface, and one of the branches occurs when there is a late infestation.
potato/insect.2.appearance: Infestation by the mole cricket begins from the start of planting the seed tubers until harvest, and infestation by the mole cricket is more frequent in the summer potato season than in the winter season, and the infestation increases in light soils and organically fertilised soils.
potato/insect.2.timing: When feeding tunnels are seen inside the rows after irrigation; it is worth noting that flooding the soil with water helps the mole cricket to come out.

potato/insect.3.name: Whitefly
potato/insect.3.symptom: Curling and yellowing of the leaves - the immature stages can be seen using a 10x lens - appearance of honeydew when the infestation increases - stunting and deformation of the plants and their failure to mature.
potato/insect.3.timing: When the numbers reach 5 insects per leaf in the leaves examined in the laboratory.
potato/insect.3.guidance: Care should be taken to cover the treated plants completely with the spray liquid, and to repeat the spraying when necessary.

potato/insect.4.name: Aphids
potato/insect.4.symptom: Appearance of pale yellow spots - curling and rolling of the leaves - honeydew - wilting, drying and death of the leaves - presence of nymphs and winged individuals - appearance of virus-infected plants after infestation by aphids.
potato/insect.4.appearance: They begin to appear from February until April, during the summer season.
potato/insect.4.timing: Preventive treatment is necessary, since the adults of the peach aphid are a main vector of the viral leaf roll disease and of virus Y in potatoes.
potato/insect.4.guidance: Treatment is carried out with the recommended pesticide when any numbers of the insect are present on the plant. Both surfaces of the leaves must be covered with the spray solution.

potato/insect.5.name: Potato tuber moth (in the field)
potato/insect.5.symptom: Appearance of large, flattened tunnels between the two surfaces of the leaf; these tunnels look silvery and transparent and are caused by the larvae of the insect. It also infests exposed tubers close to the soil surface in the field, where the larvae enter the tubers and make tunnels starting from the eyes of the tubers and continuing inward.
potato/insect.5.appearance: The infestation appears during the period from April to November of each year, and the most heavily infested seasons are the plantings of the summer and late summer seasons.
potato/insect.5.timing: When the infestation reaches 5% of the plants examined at random.
potato/insect.5.guidance: Spraying is carried out on the foliage before sunset, with repeated spraying when necessary.

potato/insect.6.name: Cotton leafworm
potato/insect.6.symptom: Presence of egg masses on the leaves - feeding of the larvae on the growing tips and presence of holes in the leaves.
potato/insect.6.appearance: October and November plantings during the Nile and winter seasons.
potato/insect.6.timing: When areas infested with egg masses and recent hatching appear.
potato/insect.6.guidance: Treatment is carried out after irrigation, once the soil can bear walking on it, as a spray on the foliage.

potato/mite.7.name: Red spider mite
potato/mite.7.symptom: Presence of yellowed plants in the middle of the field - appearance of yellow or brown spots on the leaf surface that soon cover the whole leaf - roughness of the yellowed leaf surface - wilting and drying of the leaves.
potato/mite.7.appearance: The infestation appears in summer potatoes during April, and in Nile potatoes in early September.
potato/mite.7.timing: When the average number of mites reaches 5 individuals per leaf of the leaves examined at random.
potato/mite.7.guidance: The plants are sprayed, covering the lower surface of the leaves.

potato/fungus.8.name: Black scurf (soil-borne fungi)
potato/fungus.8.symptom: Dark brown cankers surrounding the stem partially or completely above the soil surface. Dark spots form on the infected tubers, with the presence of black sclerotia (stony bodies).
potato/fungus.8.timing: Treatment of the tubers before planting.

potato/fungus.9.name: Root rot and damping-off
potato/fungus.9.symptom: Infection occurs on seedlings before or after germination or on whole plants, and causes cankers and rotting on the root, and the root system decays and dies, which causes yellowing and wilting symptoms to appear on the foliage above the soil surface, and causes stunting of the plants and a reduction in productivity.
potato/fungus.9.appearance: At the beginning of the plant's life and at any stage of the plant's growth.
potato/fungus.9.timing: Treatment of the tubers before planting.

potato/fungus.10.name: Fusarium wilt
potato/fungus.10.symptom: Symptoms begin in older plants with yellowing of the leaves, and the symptoms are often characterised by yellowing of only one side of the leaf or branch. The infected leaves wilt and die, and infected plants become stunted, and the older leaves and plants turn yellow and wilt. The disease develops with a characteristic red or brown discolouration of the vascular bundle tissue in infected plants, which can be seen if the main stem is cut lengthwise or when a branch of the main stem is cut. The discolouration of the vascular bundles may extend throughout the main stem and the lateral branches.
potato/fungus.10.appearance: At the beginning of the plant's life and at any stage of the plant's growth.
potato/fungus.10.timing: Treatment of the tubers before planting.

potato/fungus.11.name: Sclerotinia white mould
potato/fungus.11.symptom: Symptoms appear on any part of the plant, especially on the stem near the soil surface, and the infection is in the form of small, small water-soaked spots that later turn brown; the infection may extend downward to infect the root system and also extends up the stem until it reaches the bases and the ... of the leaves, causing their yellowing and wilting. The spots on the stem and branches may turn into cankers and the growth of the white cottony fungus appears, and the infected tissues become soft, bad pink or brown in colour, covered with white cottony ..., with the start of the appearance of masses of dense fungal growth distributed irregularly on the infected tissues, which are the beginnings of the formation of the stony bodies (sclerotia); finally these stony bodies take on a black colour, and their length ranges between 2 cm - 1 cm or more, and their shapes are irregular.
potato/fungus.11.appearance: When suitable conditions are available, especially high relative humidity and low temperatures.
potato/fungus.11.timing: Treatment of the tubers before planting.

potato/fungus.12.name: Dry rot
potato/fungus.12.symptom: The first symptoms of dry rot appear on the tubers as sunken areas on the outer surface of the tuber, and as the infection progresses the outer skin of the tuber wrinkles and death of the tissues occurs beneath this area, and the symptoms on the inner parts of the tuber are in the form of a cankered area of dark black or brown colour. These parts often dry out and separate from the rest of the tuber, and the fungus enters the tuber and causes rotting in the middle of the tuber, and this infected area appears in the form of a cavity, and these cavities are often covered with mycelium and fungal spores of different colours, either yellow or purple, and in the end the infected tuber loses its water and becomes dry, shrivelled and hard.
potato/fungus.12.timing: Treatment of the tubers before storage.

potato/fungus.13.name: Early blight
potato/fungus.13.symptom: Symptoms appear in the form of regularly shaped round brown spots with concentric rings inside the spots, which appear clearly when the leaves are exposed to sunlight, and symptoms also appear on the stem in the form of longitudinal brown spots.
potato/fungus.13.appearance: When weather conditions are suitable, 25 to 30 degrees Celsius, with high relative humidity.
potato/fungus.13.timing: When the symptoms of the disease start to appear

potato/fungus.14.name: Late blight
potato/fungus.14.symptom: Disease symptoms appear on the leaves in the form of irregular grey spots surrounded by a yellow or greenish-yellow halo, and on the lower surface of these spots there is a white or grey downy growth consisting of the spore-bearing stalks (sporangiophores) of the causal fungus; the infection on the leaf petioles and stems is in the form of longitudinal grey spots, and in severe infection the stems break when there is a strong air current or strong winds.
potato/fungus.14.appearance: When the plants in the field touch each other, with high humidity and low temperature.
potato/fungus.14.timing: When the infection appears, especially in the Nile season or in sprinkler-irrigated areas.
potato/fungus.14.guidance: It is necessary for the spray solution to cover both the upper and lower surfaces of the leaves.

potato/nematode.15.name: Root-knot nematode
potato/nematode.15.symptom: 1. There are general symptoms on infected plants such as the presence of galls (swellings) of various sizes and shapes, which leads to weakness and stunting of the plants and yellowing of their leaves. 2. These symptoms appear in the field in the form of groups of plants in scattered patches depending on the severity of infection. 3. There are also symptoms on the tubers, and the tubers appear full of pustules, and on the inside tissue of the tuber there are dark brown spots.
potato/nematode.15.appearance: With the spread of the root system and the formation of tubers.
potato/nematode.15.timing: At planting, and detecting any population in the soil at the start of the season is considered dangerous and treatment must begin immediately.

potato/other.16.name: Soil sterilisation in open fields
potato/other.16.symptom: 1. Presence of galls (swellings) of various sizes and shapes, which leads to weakness, stunting and yellowing of the plants. 2. These symptoms appear in the field in the form of groups of plants in scattered patches depending on the severity of infection.
potato/other.16.appearance: With the spread of the root system and the formation of tubers.
potato/other.16.timing: Sterilising the soil about one month before planting, when the root-knot index is at least 2 in the previous crop.

potato/nematode.17.name: Lesion nematode
potato/nematode.17.symptom: Presence of cankers on the secondary roots.
potato/nematode.17.guidance: The pesticide is used at planting by pinching (hand-applying a pinch) together with the seed tubers, followed immediately by irrigation.

sweet-potato/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
sweet-potato/insect.1.symptom: First-instar larvae feed on the lower surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe with the presence of older larvae, they feed, making holes in the leaves and causing their damage.
sweet-potato/insect.1.timing: When infestation is seen in the field.

sweet-potato/insect.2.name: Whitefly
sweet-potato/insect.2.symptom: The whitefly causes damage to the leaves through feeding; the infestation occurs on the lower surface of the leaves, and the insect sucks the plant sap to feed, which leads to the leaves turning yellow and curling, then the leaves appearing shiny or black. The feeding of the whitefly on the sweet potato plant is considered particularly harmful because it causes uneven ripening of the tubers.
sweet-potato/insect.2.timing: When the numbers reach 5 insects per leaf in the leaves examined in the laboratory.

sweet-potato/mite.3.name: Red spider mite
sweet-potato/mite.3.symptom: Appearance of spots on the upper surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe, spider webs form on the lower surface of the leaves and the leaves turn yellow and fall; feeding on the sap leads to weakness and drying of the plant, which leads to the falling of the leaves and buds and of the whole plant. The infestation appears in the summer season in April and in the Nile season in early September.
sweet-potato/mite.3.appearance: The months of May and June until the end of the season.
sweet-potato/mite.3.timing: It can begin at the seedling stage when 3 - 4 individuals are present on the plant, and at the vegetative growth and flowering stage when there is an average of 4 individuals per leaf of the total leaves examined at random.

sweet-potato/fungus.4.name: Root rots
sweet-potato/fungus.4.symptom: Infection occurs on the shoot of the potato sprouting from one of the eyes of the potato tuber, and the disease may cause death of the shoot above the ground or shortly after its emergence, and another shoot may grow from other eyes to compensate for the death of the other shoots.
sweet-potato/fungus.4.appearance: At the beginning of the plant's life and at any stage of the plant's growth.
sweet-potato/fungus.4.timing: Treatment of the tubers before planting.

carrot/mite.1.name: Red spider mite
carrot/mite.1.symptom: Appearance of spots on the upper surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe, spider webs form on the lower surface of the leaves and the leaves turn yellow and fall.
carrot/mite.1.appearance: Mid-March to mid-May and until the end of the season.
carrot/mite.1.timing: It can begin at the seedling stage when 3-4 individuals are present on the plant, and at the vegetative growth and flowering stage when there is an average of 4 individuals per leaf of the total leaves examined at random.

carrot/fungus.2.name: Powdery mildew
carrot/fungus.2.symptom: Symptoms appear in the form of white powdery spots on the leaves and petioles of the carrot and on the buds and flowers, which then turn yellow and twist, and finally this leads to their falling.
carrot/fungus.2.appearance: When suitable conditions of warm temperature and moderate humidity are available.
carrot/fungus.2.timing: At the start of the appearance of the disease symptoms.

carrot/nematode.3.name: Root-knot nematode
carrot/nematode.3.symptom: The infestation causes twisting, deformation and branching of the roots, as it damages the tip of the growing root, resulting in forked or deformed roots; the deformed roots tend to have soil sticking to them, and branching is sometimes seen in several directions; in severe infestation, irregularly shaped balls appear outside the root, and infected plants can be pulled from the soil easily; among the symptoms of infestation of the plants are stunting and weak growth and then their yellowing and wilting.
carrot/nematode.3.guidance: The pesticide is added to the soil immediately before irrigation.

leafbeet/insect.1.name: Aphids
leafbeet/insect.1.symptom: The aphid sucks the plant sap through its piercing-sucking mouthparts and secretes honeydew, and the infestation leads to curling and deformation of the leaves, especially the terminal growth.
leafbeet/insect.1.timing: As soon as the symptoms of infestation appear, and preventive spraying is necessary.

pepper/insect.1.name: Thrips
pepper/insect.1.symptom: The thrips individuals feed on the leaves, buds and fruits, causing white - light silvery spots; these spots turn black. The thrips also cause the flowers to fall and not to form.
pepper/insect.1.timing: When individuals begin to appear on the leaves and flowers.
pepper/insect.1.guidance: Agricultural sanitation and getting rid of weeds, with the use of blue sticky traps to detect the presence of the pest.

pepper/insect.2.name: Whitefly
pepper/insect.2.symptom: Presence of adult insects on the lower surface of the leaves, and yellow spots appear at the start of the infestation resulting from piercing and sucking, followed by yellowing and curling of the leaves as a result of the viral infection. As the infestation progresses, stunting of the plants, roughness of the leaves and ease of their breaking occur, followed by a decrease in yield. Honeydew also appears when the infestation is severe.
pepper/insect.2.appearance: In the late summer season, and it intensifies in the Nile season from the month of August until the month of December.
pepper/insect.2.timing: When infestation by nymphs on the leaves is discovered, or when 2 adult insects/plant are discovered in the plants examined at random.

pepper/insect.3.name: Aphids
pepper/insect.3.symptom: Curling of the leaves and growing tips and appearance of yellow spots on the leaves then their wilting - deformation of the plants, especially the growing tips and young leaves, with the appearance of viral diseases.
pepper/insect.3.appearance: March and April - August and September.
pepper/insect.3.timing: When there is an average of 1 - 2 individuals per leaf in the leaves examined at random.
pepper/insect.3.guidance: Treatment is carried out by spraying the plants, covering the treated plants completely with the spray liquid.

pepper/insect.4.name: Cotton leafworm
pepper/insect.4.symptom: The newly hatched larvae feed on the leaf epidermis around the egg-mass site and the feeding widens until it covers the leaf surface, and the leaf appears thin and transparent and then dries; holes also occur in it, in addition to the buds, flowers and small fruit set, and the larva makes tunnels inside the fruits and the opening of the tunnel is irregular.
pepper/insect.4.timing: When feeding traces of the larvae are seen and a 5 % infestation rate is present

pepper/mite.5.name: Red spider mite
pepper/mite.5.symptom: Appearance of silvery spots on the upper surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe, spider webs form on the lower surface of the leaves and the leaves turn yellow and fall.
pepper/mite.5.appearance: Mid-March to mid-May and until the end of the season.
pepper/mite.5.timing: It can begin at the seedling stage when 3-4 individuals are present on the plant, and at the vegetative growth and flowering stage when there is an average of 4 individuals per leaf of the total leaves examined at random.

pepper/fungus.6.name: Powdery mildew
pepper/fungus.6.symptom: Yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaf, corresponding on the lower surface to fine white growths; the leaves turn brown and die when the infestation becomes severe.
pepper/fungus.6.appearance: When the environmental conditions suitable for the appearance of the infection are available.
pepper/fungus.6.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.
pepper/fungus.6.guidance: The spray solution must cover both the upper and lower surfaces of the leaves.

pepper/fungus.7.name: Grey mould
pepper/fungus.7.symptom: The infection usually begins on the flowers, small fruit set and small fruits in the form of olive-coloured growth, and then the flowers and small fruits soon dry and fall; as the infection progresses the fruits become infected in the form of soft, water-soaked-looking, irregularly shaped spots of olive-green colour that lose their firmness, and the grey powdery spores of the fungus appear on the surface of the infected tissue; these spots soon increase in area and extend to the remaining healthy parts of the fruit within a short period when conditions suitable for the fungus are available and it is not controlled
pepper/fungus.7.appearance: When suitable conditions are available, especially high relative humidity and moderate temperatures.
pepper/fungus.7.timing: At the start of the appearance of the disease symptoms on the flowers and fruits.

eggplant/insect.1.name: Whitefly
eggplant/insect.1.symptom: The adult insects and nymphs feed on eggplant leaves and all stages are found on the lower surface of the leaves, feeding in groups, and as a result of the feeding spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves until they turn yellow and curl in the case of virus transmission as a result of sap sucking.
eggplant/insect.1.appearance: April for the early seasons and from June to October for the late seasons.
eggplant/insect.1.timing: When the average infestation reaches 10 adult insects or 20 nymphs per leaf.

eggplant/mite.2.name: Red spider mite
eggplant/mite.2.symptom: Appearance of yellow to brown spots on the leaves. Yellowing and wilting of the leaves. Drying of the leaves and their falling in cases of severe infestation and dry weather.
eggplant/mite.2.timing: When the average number of mites reaches 5 individuals per leaf in the leaves examined at random.
eggplant/mite.2.guidance: The pesticide solution is sprayed on the plants, covering the lower surface of the leaves.

cucumber/insect.1.name: Whitefly
cucumber/insect.1.symptom: Presence of adult insects on the lower surface of the leaves, and at the start of the infestation yellow spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves, and the immature stages (nymphs) can be seen using a ×10 field lens; also, increased infestation leads to curling of the leaves and then their wilting, and yellowing and weakness of the plant.
cucumber/insect.1.appearance: From May to November, i.e. during the late summer, Nile and early winter seasons.
cucumber/insect.1.timing: At an average of 5 adult insects per leaf in the leaves examined at random.
cucumber/insect.1.guidance: Treatment is carried out as a general spray on the plants, and care is taken to cover the treated plants completely with the spray liquid and to repeat the spraying when necessary.

cucumber/insect.2.name: Aphids
cucumber/insect.2.symptom: Curling of the leaves and growing tips and appearance of yellow spots on the leaves then their wilting - deformation of the plants, especially the growing tips and young leaves - appearance and spread of viral diseases.
cucumber/insect.2.appearance: March and April - August and September.
cucumber/insect.2.timing: When there is an average of 1-2 individuals per leaf in the leaves examined at random.
cucumber/insect.2.guidance: Treatment is carried out by spraying the plants, covering the treated plants completely with the spray solution.

cucumber/insect.3.name: Leafminers
cucumber/insect.3.symptom: The larvae feed between the two epidermal layers of the leaf, forming thin, winding mines that gradually widen and at their ends form patches free of leaf tissue, transparent in colour, turning brown as a result of the death of the epidermal cells.
cucumber/insect.3.appearance: October and November - March and April.
cucumber/insect.3.timing: When there are 2-3 mines/leaf in the leaves examined at random.
cucumber/insect.3.guidance: Spraying is carried out on the foliage of the plants.

cucumber/insect.4.name: Cotton leafworm
cucumber/insect.4.symptom: The larvae feed on the lower surface of the leaves making holes, and when the infestation becomes severe they feed on the whole leaf and cause damage to the foliage, and they feed on the cucumber fruits, where they feed on the epidermis of the green fruits.
cucumber/insect.4.appearance: From the beginning of seedling emergence until the end of the season.
cucumber/insect.4.timing: When signs of infestation are seen on the leaves.

cucumber/mite.5.name: Red spider mite
cucumber/mite.5.symptom: Appearance of yellow to brown spots on the leaves. Yellowing and wilting of the leaves. Drying of the leaves and their falling in cases of severe infestation and dry weather.
cucumber/mite.5.appearance: Summer cucumber: April and May - Nile cucumber: the months of July and August.
cucumber/mite.5.timing: When the average number of mites reaches 5-7 individuals per leaf in the leaves examined at random.
cucumber/mite.5.guidance: The plants are sprayed, covering the lower surface of the leaves.

cucumber/fungus.6.name: Fruit rots
cucumber/fungus.6.symptom: Hard, sunken spots form on the fruits, whose colour differs according to the causal pathogen, in the areas where the fruits touch the soil or are exposed to high humidity.
cucumber/fungus.6.appearance: The symptoms appear when weather conditions of moderate temperature and high humidity are available, from the month of September.

cucumber/fungus.7.name: Root rot and damping-off
cucumber/fungus.7.symptom: It is caused by numerous fungi and results in the absence of hills (planting spots) in the early period of the plant's life, before germination or after their emergence above the soil surface, leading to a shortage of plants in the field.
cucumber/fungus.7.appearance: At the seedling age stage of 21 - 30 days.
cucumber/fungus.7.timing: Treatment of the seeds before planting - or treatment of the seedlings or the soil after planting.
cucumber/fungus.7.guidance: The soil is treated with the pesticide as a spray around the seedlings, and care must be taken with irrigation and not to overdo it.

cucumber/fungus.8.name: Powdery mildew
cucumber/fungus.8.symptom: Pale or yellow spots on the leaves covered with a white powdery dust; the spots widen and cover both surfaces of the leaf, which dries and then dies.
cucumber/fungus.8.appearance: It appears after about 30-35 from planting.
cucumber/fungus.8.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

cucumber/fungus.9.name: Downy mildew
cucumber/fungus.9.symptom: Angular yellow spots on the leaves that widen quickly and merge, and on the lower surface of these spots a grey downy growth appears.
cucumber/fungus.9.appearance: At any age of plant growth.
cucumber/fungus.9.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.
cucumber/fungus.9.guidance: Care should be taken that the spray solution reaches both the upper and lower surfaces of the leaves.

cucumber/fungus.10.name: Gummy stem blight
cucumber/fungus.10.symptom: The disease causes rapid death of small plants if the hypocotyl (embryonic stalk) or the cotyledons are infected. On older plants, round spots of dark red to black colour appear, reaching about 5 mm in diameter, sometimes surrounded by a yellow halo. The infection can begin from the leaf margins in the form of wilting that advances inward toward the centre of the leaf, finally causing leaf blight. Cankers appear on the stem and branches, and longitudinal cracks of brown colour from which gummy exudates of red or reddish-brown colour ooze, sometimes with small black fruiting bodies of the fungus immersed in them. This exposure can manifest in the crown region of the plant; finally shrivelling and girdling of these areas occurs and death of the plant vines above the infected area. With the appearance on the fruits of small, semi-water-soaked, round to oval spots of brown colour that turn black, gummy exudates and black fungal bodies may appear on these spots as distinctive and confirmatory signs of this disease.
cucumber/fungus.10.appearance: At any stage of plant growth, especially at the beginning of life.
cucumber/fungus.10.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

cucumber/nematode.11.name: Root-knot nematode
cucumber/nematode.11.symptom: Symptoms of nematode infestation appear among the cucumber plants at all growth stages in the form of yellow spots, stunting and absence of hills irregularly in the field, similar to the symptoms of nutrient deficiency and infections by both types of mildew diseases; when the plants are uprooted, nematode galls (tumours) are observed on the roots.
cucumber/nematode.11.appearance: Symptoms begin from the seedling stage until fruiting.
cucumber/nematode.11.timing: With planting of the seedling or at most one week after planting it, to ensure protection of the plant, especially in the presence of even small numbers of root-knot nematode.

koosa/insect.1.name: Whitefly
koosa/insect.1.symptom: Adults and nymphs feed on squash leaves, and all stages are found on the lower surface of the leaves, feeding in groups; as a result of feeding, yellow spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves until they turn yellow and curl, in the case of virus transmission, as a result of sap sucking.

koosa/fungus.2.name: Powdery mildew
koosa/fungus.2.symptom: Fine white spots on both surfaces of the leaf that turn brown and dry out as the infestation progresses, and rarely appear on the fruits. Severe infection leads to the death of the leaves.
koosa/fungus.2.timing: At the onset of the appearance of symptoms.

pumpkin/fungus.1.name: Powdery mildew
pumpkin/fungus.1.symptom: Presence of fine white spots on both surfaces of the leaf, then these spots turn brown and dry out, and these spots rarely form on the fruits; the severity of infection leads to the death of the infected leaves, so the plant weakens and its size decreases, and the fruits exposed to the sun ripen early because most of the leaves have died, and the yield is reduced in the end.
pumpkin/fungus.1.appearance: The disease spreads during the season in warm weather and high atmospheric humidity.

pumpkin/fungus.2.name: Downy mildew
pumpkin/fungus.2.symptom: Appearance of pale or yellow spots of limited (angular) shape on the upper surface of the infected leaves, corresponding on the lower surface of the leaf to a purple or white down, which is the spore-bearing structures (sporangiophores) of the fungus; when the infection intensifies, the leaves die, the plant weakens, its yield decreases and its fruits become small in size.
pumpkin/fungus.2.appearance: When low temperatures and high humidity are available.

koosa_labb/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
koosa_labb/insect.1.symptom: As soon as the egg masses hatch, first-instar larvae begin feeding on the lower surface of the leaves, and as the larval instars advance and the infestation worsens, the advanced larvae feed on the entire leaf, causing holes and damage to the foliage.
koosa_labb/insect.1.appearance: From the seedling stage until harvest.
koosa_labb/insect.1.timing: When signs of infestation are observed on the leaves.

watermelon/mite.1.name: Red spider mite
watermelon/mite.1.symptom: Appearance of yellow to brown spots on the leaf surface, especially in the lobed areas near the midrib. Wilting and curling of the leaves, and yellowing and drying of the leaves when the infestation is severe.
watermelon/mite.1.appearance: Starting from the month of May.
watermelon/mite.1.timing: When the average number of mites reaches 5 motile individuals on both surfaces of the leaf, in leaves examined at random.
watermelon/mite.1.guidance: Plants are sprayed while covering the lower surface of the leaves.

watermelon/fungus.2.name: Powdery mildew
