watermelon/fungus.2.symptom: The infection appears in the form of irregular yellow-brown spots on the upper surface of the leaves; as the infection progresses the spots spread on both surfaces of the leaf, and in the early morning the spots on the lower surface of the leaf turn grey and these spots disappear in dry weather, then the spots increase in size and turn black and cover the entire leaf surface, which leads to the death of the infected leaves.
watermelon/fungus.2.appearance: The disease appears at all stages of plant growth if suitable conditions of humidity and temperature are available.
watermelon/fungus.2.timing: Spraying is carried out at the onset of the appearance of infection, provided that the spray solution covers the lower and upper surfaces of the leaf.

watermelon/fungus.3.name: Downy mildew
watermelon/fungus.3.symptom: The infection appears in the form of pale yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves, corresponding on the lower surface to a grey downy growth that then turns dark or blackish, consisting of the spore-bearing structures (sporangiophores) of the fungus that causes the disease, emerging from the pustules.
watermelon/fungus.3.appearance: This disease appears at all stages of plant growth if suitable conditions of humidity and temperature are available.
watermelon/fungus.3.timing: Spraying is carried out at the onset of the appearance of infection, provided that the spray solution covers the lower and upper surfaces of the leaf.

watermelon/fungus.4.name: Gummy stem blight
watermelon/fungus.4.symptom: The disease causes rapid death of small plants if the hypocotyl (embryonic stalk) or the cotyledons are infected. On older plants, round spots of dark red to black colour appear, reaching about 5 mm in diameter, sometimes surrounded by a yellow halo. The infection can begin from the leaf margins in the form of wilting that advances inward toward the centre of the leaf, finally causing leaf blight. Cankers appear on the stem and branches, and longitudinal cracks of brown colour from which gummy exudates of red or reddish-brown colour ooze, sometimes with small black fruiting bodies of the fungus immersed in them. This exposure can manifest in the crown region of the plant; finally shrivelling and girdling of these areas occurs and death of the plant vines above the infected area. With the appearance on the fruits of small, semi-water-soaked, round to oval spots of brown colour that turn black, gummy exudates and black fungal bodies may appear on these spots as distinctive and confirmatory signs of this disease.
watermelon/fungus.4.appearance: At any stage of plant growth, especially at the beginning of life.
watermelon/fungus.4.timing: At the onset of the appearance of symptoms.

melo_labb/insect.1.name: Aphids
melo_labb/insect.1.symptom: The aphid sucks plant sap through its piercing-sucking mouthparts and secretes honeydew on which black mould fungi grow, affecting photosynthesis, and the infestation leads to curling and deformation of the plants, especially the terminal growth.
melo_labb/insect.1.timing: When 10 - 15 wingless individuals are present per 10 plants examined at random.

melo_labb/insect.2.name: Cotton leafworm
melo_labb/insect.2.symptom: First-instar larvae feed on the lower surface of the leaves, and as the larva ages it feeds on the leaves causing holes in them, then causes damage to the foliage when the infestation intensifies.
melo_labb/insect.2.appearance: When seedlings emerge, the larvae feed on tender tissues, until the end of harvest.
melo_labb/insect.2.timing: When signs of infestation are observed.

melo_labb/insect.3.name: Whitefly
melo_labb/insect.3.symptom: Adults and nymphs feed on the leaves by sucking sap, and all stages are found on the lower surface of the leaf, causing spots that appear on the upper surface of the leaves, which then turn yellow and curl.
melo_labb/insect.3.timing: When the average infestation reaches 10 adults or 20 nymphs per leaf from plants examined at random.

melo_labb/mite.4.name: Red spider mite
melo_labb/mite.4.symptom: Silvery or bronze spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves as a result of sap sucking; when the infestation becomes severe, webs form and the leaves curl and dry.
melo_labb/mite.4.appearance: From the emergence of seedlings until harvest.
melo_labb/mite.4.timing: At the seedling stage when there is an average of 3 - 4 individuals per plant in samples examined at random, or as soon as symptoms of infestation appear at any stage.

melo_labb/fungus.5.name: Powdery mildew
melo_labb/fungus.5.symptom: Symptoms begin first on the old leaves and on their lower surface, then move to the young leaves; the infection takes the form of fine grey spots, and as the infection progresses the symptoms appear on the upper surface and the size of the spots increases until they spread over the whole leaf, and the leaf colour turns dark as the infection becomes severe, then the leaf dries and falls; the infection leads to shrivelling and small size of the fruits and consequently to poor quality.
melo_labb/fungus.5.appearance: The disease spreads during the season in warm weather and high atmospheric humidity.

melo_labb/fungus.6.name: Gummy stem blight
melo_labb/fungus.6.symptom: The disease causes rapid death of young plants, and on large plants round dark red spots appear with a diameter of up to 5 mm surrounded by a yellow halo, where the infection starts from the leaf margins as a wilting that progresses inward toward the centre of the leaf, causing the appearance of blight on the leaves; cankers appear on the stem and branches and brown longitudinal cracks from which gummy exudates of red or reddish-brown colour flow, sometimes with the small black fruiting bodies of the fungus embedded in them.
melo_labb/fungus.6.appearance: This disease appears at all stages of plant growth, especially at the beginning of life.
melo_labb/fungus.6.timing: At the beginning of the appearance of the infection.

melo_labb/fungus.7.name: Downy mildew
melo_labb/fungus.7.symptom: The infection appears as pale yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves, opposite which on the lower surface is a grey downy growth that then turns dark or blackened, consisting of the spore-bearing structures of the causal fungus emerging from the pustules.
melo_labb/fungus.7.appearance: The disease appears at all stages of plant growth if suitable conditions of humidity and temperature are available.
melo_labb/fungus.7.timing: Spraying is carried out at the beginning of the appearance of the infection, provided that the spray solution covers the lower and upper surfaces of the leaf.

melon/fungus.1.name: Powdery mildew
melon/fungus.1.symptom: Pale yellow spots on the leaves, petioles and stems covered with the powdery white spores of the fungus, which turn yellow then brown, and the leaves dry and die when the infection becomes severe.
melon/fungus.1.appearance: This disease appears at all stages of plant growth if suitable conditions of high relative humidity and moderate temperature (25-30°) are available.
melon/fungus.1.timing: Spraying is carried out at the beginning of the appearance of the symptoms of infection.

melon/fungus.2.name: Gummy stem blight
melon/fungus.2.symptom: Small round or irregularly shaped spots, purple to black, appear on the cotyledons and the stem of the seedling; the disease appears on large plants at about the middle of the growing season in the form of central purple spots that turn dark brown on the leaves, and when the fungal spores spread they infect large plants at the branching point of the stem, resulting in dark brown or black cankers on the stem containing black fruiting bodies, accompanied by gummy exudates. The lower leaves dry first, then wilting and drying of the leaves spreads from the bottom upward until the whole foliage dies. Water-soaked spots form on the fruits; these spots expand to an unlimited size and cause a sunken rot in the fruit, and gummy exudates and black fruiting bodies also appear on them.
melon/fungus.2.appearance: During the plant growth period, especially in the early stages of growth.
melon/fungus.2.guidance: The disease spreads generally in warm and hot regions and when high humidity is available.

cantaloupe/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
cantaloupe/insect.1.symptom: Newly hatched larvae feed on the lower surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe with the presence of large larvae, they feed making holes in the leaves.
cantaloupe/insect.1.appearance: During March and April for the summer season.
cantaloupe/insect.1.timing: With the beginning of the appearance of symptoms of infestation.

cantaloupe/insect.2.name: Whitefly
cantaloupe/insect.2.symptom: The adults and nymphs feed on cantaloupe leaves, and all stages are found on the lower surface of the leaves, feeding in groups; as a result of feeding, spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves until they turn yellow, and they curl in the case of virus transmission as a result of sap sucking.
cantaloupe/insect.2.timing: When the average infestation reaches 10 adults or 20 nymphs per leaf.

cantaloupe/insect.3.name: Melon fly
cantaloupe/insect.3.symptom: Newly hatched larvae enter the fruits and feed on the pulp and seeds and make longitudinal tunnels in the fruit, which becomes brown in colour and soft in texture, and rots and is spoiled in case of severe infestation because of bacteria and fungi. The infestation can be recognised by the presence of fine holes on the surface covered with gummy exudates, then the fruits shrivel when their infestation becomes severe.
cantaloupe/insect.3.appearance: The winter season of cantaloupe is infested.
cantaloupe/insect.3.timing: When any early infestation of 1% is detected.

cantaloupe/mite.4.name: Red spider mite
cantaloupe/mite.4.symptom: Yellow or brown spots appear on the leaf surface, especially near the midrib - yellowing and drying of the leaves when the infestation is severe.
cantaloupe/mite.4.timing: When the average number of mites reaches 5 moving individuals on both surfaces of the leaf in leaves examined at random.
cantaloupe/mite.4.guidance: The plants are sprayed while covering the lower surface of the leaves.

cantaloupe/fungus.5.name: Powdery mildew
cantaloupe/fungus.5.symptom: Pale yellow spots appear on the leaves, petioles and stems covered with the powdery white spores of the fungus, then the leaves gradually turn yellow then brown and the infected parts dry, causing the death of many leaves; these symptoms rarely appear on the fruits.
cantaloupe/fungus.5.appearance: The disease is favoured by fairly moderate temperatures and medium to high humidity levels.
cantaloupe/fungus.5.timing: At the beginning of the appearance of symptoms.
cantaloupe/fungus.5.guidance: Care should be taken not to spray sulphur compounds during times of high temperature, so that spraying can be done in the early morning or in the afternoon.

cantaloupe/fungus.6.name: Downy mildew
cantaloupe/fungus.6.symptom: Pale yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves, opposite which on the lower surface is a grey downy growth at first that then turns dark or blackened, consisting of the spore-bearing structures of the causal fungus emerging from the stomata.
cantaloupe/fungus.6.appearance: At any stage of plant growth.
cantaloupe/fungus.6.timing: At the beginning of the appearance of symptoms.
cantaloupe/fungus.6.guidance: The spray solution must reach both the upper and lower surfaces of the leaves.

cantaloupe/fungus.7.name: Root rot and damping-off
cantaloupe/fungus.7.symptom: The infection occurs on seedlings before or after germination or on whole plants, and causes cankers and rots on the roots and decay and death of the root system, which causes yellowing and wilting symptoms on the foliage above the soil surface.
cantaloupe/fungus.7.appearance: At any stage of plant growth.
cantaloupe/fungus.7.timing: Treatment of seeds or seedlings before planting.

cantaloupe/fungus.8.name: Gummy stem blight
cantaloupe/fungus.8.symptom: The disease causes rapid death of young plants if the hypocotyl or the cotyledons are infected. On older plants, round spots of dark red to black colour appear, with a diameter of about 5 mm, sometimes surrounded by a yellow halo. The infection can start from the leaf margins as a wilting that progresses inward toward the centre of the leaf, finally causing leaf blight. Cankers appear on the stem and branches, and longitudinal cracks form, brown in colour, from which gummy exudates of red or reddish-brown colour flow, with the small black fruiting bodies of the fungus sometimes embedded in them. This symptom can appear in the crown region of the plant, and finally shrivelling and girdling of these areas occur and the vines die above the infected area. Small, round to oval, semi-watery spots, brown in colour, appear on the fruits and turn black, and gummy exudates and black fungal bodies may appear on these spots as distinctive and confirmatory signs of this disease.
cantaloupe/fungus.8.appearance: At any stage of plant growth, especially at the beginning of life.
cantaloupe/fungus.8.timing: At the beginning of the appearance of symptoms.

shahd/insect.1.name: Whitefly
shahd/insect.1.symptom: The adults and nymphs feed on shahd (honey melon) leaves, and all stages are found on the lower surface of the leaves, feeding in groups; as a result of feeding, spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves until they turn yellow, and they curl in the case of virus transmission as a result of sap sucking.
shahd/insect.1.timing: When the average infestation reaches 10 adults or 20 nymphs per leaf.

shahd/fungus.2.name: Powdery mildew
shahd/fungus.2.symptom: Presence of fine powdery white spots on both surfaces of the leaf, then these spots turn milky in colour and dry; these spots rarely form on the fruits, and severe infection leads to the death of the infected leaves, so the plant weakens and becomes small, and the fruits exposed to the sun ripen early because most leaves have died, and the yield is finally reduced.
shahd/fungus.2.appearance: The disease spreads during the season in warm weather and high atmospheric humidity.

shahd/fungus.3.name: Downy mildew
shahd/fungus.3.symptom: Pale or yellow spots of limited shape appear on the upper surface of the infected leaves, opposite which on the lower surface of the leaf is a down of purple or white colour consisting of the spore-bearing structures of the fungus, and when the infection becomes severe the leaves die and the plant weakens, its yield decreases and its fruits become small.
shahd/fungus.3.appearance: When low temperatures and high humidity are available.

bean/insect.1.name: Leafminers
bean/insect.1.symptom: Thread-like mines appear on the leaves and mines on the stem - swellings are observed at the leaf petioles and the plant stem (containing larvae and pupae).
bean/insect.1.appearance: With the beginning of the Nile season, July and August plantings.
bean/insect.1.timing: When the rate of 3-5 % is reached in leaves examined at random.

bean/insect.2.name: Aphids
bean/insect.2.symptom: Symptoms of infestation appear in the form of curling and rolling of the leaves - death of the growing tips at the seedling stage - appearance of yellow spots as a result of piercing and sucking and general weakness of the plant and wilting of the leaves and their death - with the presence of individuals and wingless nymphs and winged individuals - and honeydew with dust sticking to it and the appearance of black mould - also the appearance of mosaic diseases.
bean/insect.2.appearance: All year round, especially the summer season and the beginning of winter, and relatively less during the autumn season.
bean/insect.2.timing: When the average number of individuals of the insect reaches 6-8 nymphs/leaf in leaves examined at random.
bean/insect.2.guidance: The foliage is covered with an emphasis on the lower surface of the leaves.

bean/mite.3.name: Red spider mite
bean/mite.3.symptom: Spotting of the leaves, where yellow to brown spots appear in the midrib area - drying and wilting of the leaves - in case of severe infestation the individuals extend to the pods and scratch them, causing yellow spots.
bean/mite.3.timing: When the average number of mites reaches 5 moving individuals on both surfaces of the leaf in leaves examined at random.
bean/mite.3.guidance: The foliage is covered with an emphasis on the lower surface of the leaves.

bean/fungus.4.name: Rust
bean/fungus.4.symptom: Pustules appear on the leaf surfaces within 5 days of infection, with a diameter of 1-2 mm, white in colour and slightly raised; as the infection progresses the pustules turn reddish-brown, and as the infection continues to progress they become blackish-brown in colour, accompanied by yellowing of the infected leaves, then their drying and falling.
bean/fungus.4.appearance: The infection appears in the Nile season 30-35 days after planting.
bean/fungus.4.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

bean/fungus.5.name: Leaf spot
bean/fungus.5.symptom: Spots form on the cotyledons of young plants and the stems die as soon as they emerge above the soil surface.
bean/fungus.5.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

bean/fungus.6.name: Root rot and damping-off
bean/fungus.6.symptom: The infection occurs as root rots and damping-off early, before emergence above the soil surface, in the form of absence of hills or death of seedlings after emergence above the soil surface, and in some cases distinct constrictions appear on the seedlings with brown cankers on one side of the stem near the soil surface.
bean/fungus.6.timing: Treatment of the seed before planting.

cowpea/insect.1.name: Aphids
cowpea/insect.1.symptom: The insect sucks the plant sap with its piercing-sucking mouthparts and secretes honeydew, and the infestation leads to curling and deformation of the leaves, especially the terminal growth.
cowpea/insect.1.timing: As soon as symptoms of infestation appear, and preventive spraying is necessary.

cowpea/insect.2.name: Cowpea pod borer
cowpea/insect.2.symptom: The young larvae feed on the floral parts and the newly formed pods and cause their damage and dropping, and small black spots appear on the outside of the pod; the larvae bore inside the pods and feed on the tender seeds, the pods rot as a result of the accumulation of larval excreta inside the pods, a quantitative loss in the yield of green pods, and they also cause a decrease in the yield of dry seeds as well as their purity; holes appear on the outside of the pods as a result of the larvae exiting to pupate in the soil.
cowpea/insect.2.timing: If a severe infestation is expected, the crop is treated with the recommended pesticide at the time of flowering and fruit set to eliminate newly hatched larvae.

cowpea/insect.3.name: Whitefly
cowpea/insect.3.symptom: The adults and nymphs feed on cowpea leaves, and all stages are found on the lower surface of the leaves, feeding in groups; the result of feeding takes the form of spots that appear on the upper surface of the leaves until they turn yellow, and they curl in the case of virus transmission as a result of sap sucking.
cowpea/insect.3.timing: When 5 – 7 individuals appear on the lower surface of the leaf.

cowpea/mite.4.name: Red spider mite
cowpea/mite.4.symptom: Spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe, webs form on the lower surface of the leaves and the leaves turn yellow and fall.
cowpea/mite.4.timing: It can start at the seedling stage when 3 - 4 individuals are present on the plant, and at the vegetative growth and flowering stage when an average of 4 individuals per leaf is present out of all the leaves examined at random.

pea/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
pea/insect.1.symptom: The larvae feed on the leaves and fruits, causing holes and erosion of the leaves and deformities of the pods.
pea/insect.1.timing: At the beginning of the appearance of larvae or symptoms of infestation, and after one month from planting.
pea/insect.1.guidance: Getting rid of weeds, and not planting next to crops that are severely infested by the pest.

pea/fungus.2.name: Powdery mildew
pea/fungus.2.symptom: Symptoms of infection appear as a white to greyish fungal growth in limited areas on the lower surface of the leaf; these spots soon increase in area, join each other and cover the entire leaf surface, followed by yellowing and decay of the leaves. Surface mycelium is produced, which during its growth forms chains of conidial spores. With the progress of the disease the stems and pods are infected and the plants die, and infection of the pods leads to grey or brown discolouration of the seeds, and scattered brown spots appear on the fruits.
pea/fungus.2.appearance: The infection is favoured by warm weather and high daytime temperature for a long period, with its decrease at night to the extent that allows dew to condense on the plants in the morning, in addition to high humidity levels.
pea/fungus.2.timing: At the beginning of the appearance of the infection.

pea/fungus.3.name: Rust
pea/fungus.3.symptom: Small white pustules somewhat raised above the epidermis, which then burst and become round and reddish-brown in colour and contain a large number of urediniospores, then these pustules turn black at the end of the season, and when the infection becomes severe the plants wilt and the leaves are scorched.
pea/fungus.3.appearance: The infection spreads in early spring and is favoured by low temperature 18-25 degrees Celsius and high humidity.
pea/fungus.3.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.
pea/fungus.3.guidance: Planting resistant varieties, with care to bury plant residues in the soil quickly after harvest to get rid of the fungal spores and reduce infection in the following season.

pea/fungus.4.name: Ascochyta blight
pea/fungus.4.symptom: Large spots on the leaves, stems and pods, light brown in colour and leathery with a grey centre, then pycnidia appear as circles inside the spots - the spots may be blackened with purple margins.
pea/fungus.4.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

okra/insect.1.name: Spiny bollworm
okra/insect.1.symptom: This pest infests the cotton boll and then attacks okra fruits, which are always grown next to cotton plantings; the larvae feed on the growing tips of the okra stem, and the larvae also feed on the floral tips, which dry and die, and the larva bores into okra fruits and penetrates them and feeds on their contents and causes their damage.
okra/insect.1.appearance: When the infestation rate reaches 3 % of plants examined at random.
okra/insect.1.timing: When the okra pods appear, and the infestation may also appear in okra fruits starting from August and September.

okra/insect.2.name: Cotton leafworm
okra/insect.2.symptom: Newly hatched larvae feed on the leaf epidermis and it widens until it covers the leaf, and the leaf appears transparent, thin and perforated and finally dries, and large larvae may feed on buds, flowers and pods.
okra/insect.2.appearance: From the beginning of seedling emergence until the end of July.
okra/insect.2.timing: When signs of feeding are noticed or an infestation rate of 5 % of all plants examined at random is present.

okra/insect.3.name: Whitefly
okra/insect.3.symptom: Yellowing of okra leaves; the infestation appears in the form of yellow spots that merge with each other until they cover the leaf surface; the pest infests okra crops grown under protected cultivation and in open cultivation, and some of the pest transmits viral diseases to okra.
okra/insect.3.timing: When the average infestation reaches 10 adults or 20 nymphs per leaf from plants examined at random.

okra/mite.4.name: Red spider mite
okra/mite.4.symptom: Brown spots appear on the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe, webs form on the lower surface of the leaves and on the fruits.
okra/mite.4.appearance: In winter until the end of the season.
okra/mite.4.timing: It can start at the seedling stage when 3 - 4 individuals are present on the plant, and at the vegetative growth and flowering stage when an average of 4 individuals per leaf is present out of all the leaves examined at random.

okra/nematode.5.name: Root-knot nematode
okra/nematode.5.symptom: Its symptoms appear in the form of irregular knots or swellings whose shape varies between spherical and spindle-shaped, accompanied by swelling of the root itself in the infected area; plant growth stops and the plant's colour fades so that it looks small and stunted; symptoms of poor nutrition and thirst appear on the infected plants and the plants tend to wilt, especially in hot dry weather; small fruits often form on the infected plant.
okra/nematode.5.appearance: Symptoms of infestation begin at all stages of plant growth.
okra/nematode.5.timing: Detecting any population in the soil at the beginning of the season is considered dangerous and treatment must start immediately.

cabbage/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
cabbage/insect.1.symptom: The larvae feed on the leaves, making holes, with the presence of insect excrement.
cabbage/insect.1.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.
cabbage/insect.1.guidance: The plants are sprayed while covering the lower surface of the leaves.

cabbage/insect.2.name: Whitefly
cabbage/insect.2.symptom: The adults and nymphs feed on cabbage leaves, and all stages are found on the lower surface of the leaves, feeding in groups; as a result of feeding, spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves until they turn yellow, and they curl in the case of virus transmission as a result of sap sucking.
cabbage/insect.2.timing: When individuals are seen on the lower surface of the leaves.

cabbage/insect.3.name: Aphids
cabbage/insect.3.symptom: The aphid sucks the plant sap with its piercing-sucking mouthparts and secretes honeydew on which black mould fungi grow, affecting the process of photosynthesis, and the infestation leads to curling and deformation of the leaves, especially the terminal growth.
cabbage/insect.3.timing: When an average of 25 insects per leaf is present.

cabbage/insect.4.name: Cabbage white butterfly
cabbage/insect.4.symptom: First-instar larvae feed irregularly on the margins of the first leaves, and also feed on the surface layer of the cabbage stem, and after the larvae reach advanced instars they begin feeding on parts of the leaf making holes; the larvae are seen in large numbers in the heart of the infested plant, and larval excrement is seen in large amounts in the leaf axils, and the larvae also dig tunnels inside cabbage heads, leading to the growth of the microorganisms that cause rots.
cabbage/insect.4.appearance: The butterflies appear in spring and lay eggs on the lower surface of the leaves, and the eggs hatch after 7 - 9 days during winter and after 3 days in summer.
cabbage/insect.4.timing: When one butterfly is seen or 2 larvae per plant are present.

cabbage/insect.5.name: Diamondback moth
cabbage/insect.5.symptom: The young larvae crawl upon hatching to the lower side of the leaf where they make tunnels inside it or dig tunnels in its large veins; severe infestation may lead to the death of young plants, and as the larva advances in age it makes various holes in the leaves. The larvae prefer the tender leaves of the plants, especially the heart leaves; the larvae spin silken threads to live beneath them while feeding, and the infestation varies from one season to another, and when seedlings or young plants are severely infested this may lead to their death.
cabbage/insect.5.timing: As soon as the infestation appears.

cabbage/mite.6.name: Red spider mite
cabbage/mite.6.symptom: Yellow spots appear on the upper surface of the leaves - roughness of the leaf surface and its curling in the areas where individuals are present, wilting and drying of the leaves.
cabbage/mite.6.timing: As soon as the infestation appears.

cabbage/fungus.7.name: Downy mildew
cabbage/fungus.7.symptom: Pale yellow spots appear on the upper surface of the leaf, opposite which is a grey downy growth on the lower surface; with time the infection spreads and the leaves die, dry and fall.
cabbage/fungus.7.appearance: The disease spreads when high humidity is available.

cabbage/fungus.8.name: Powdery mildew
cabbage/fungus.8.symptom: Symptoms appear in the form of white powdery spots on the leaves and petioles of carrot and on the buds and flowers, then the leaves turn yellow and twist and finally this leads to their falling.
cabbage/fungus.8.appearance: When suitable conditions of warm temperature and moderate humidity are available.
cabbage/fungus.8.timing: At the start of the appearance of the disease symptoms.

cabbage/fungus.9.name: Root rot and damping-off
cabbage/fungus.9.symptom: The disease causes rot and death of seeds before their emergence above the soil surface, causing the absence of many hills in the nursery, or the seedlings in the nursery are infected, leading to the death of many seedlings in the nursery. Infection of large plants rarely leads to the death of the plant, but a severe shortage occurs in the roots that carry water and food, leading to wilting of the plant, stunting of the leaves and their turning yellow.
cabbage/fungus.9.appearance: At the beginning of the plant's life and at any stage of plant growth.
cabbage/fungus.9.timing: Treatment of seeds in the nursery or treatment of seedlings before planting in the permanent field.

broccoli/insect.1.name: Cabbage white butterfly
broccoli/insect.1.symptom: The larvae gnaw the leaf margins irregularly, and also feed on the surface layer of the broccoli stem, and the advanced instars attack the host leaves, beginning to feed on parts of the leaf; the larvae are seen in large numbers in the heart of the infested plant, and larval excrement is seen in large amounts in the leaf axils, and the larvae live in groups, and the larvae also dig tunnels inside cabbage heads, leading to the growth of the microorganisms that cause rots.
broccoli/insect.1.appearance: Starting from the month of October.
broccoli/insect.1.timing: When one butterfly is seen or 2 larvae per plant are present.

broccoli/insect.2.name: Cotton leafworm
broccoli/insect.2.symptom: The larvae feed on the leaves, making holes and with the presence of larval excrement.
broccoli/insect.2.appearance: During October and November and also in March and April.
broccoli/insect.2.timing: At the start of the appearance of symptoms of infestation.

cauliflower/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
cauliflower/insect.1.symptom: First-instar larvae feed on the lower surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe with the presence of larvae of older instars, they feed making holes in the leaves and cause their damage.
cauliflower/insect.1.timing: With the beginning of the appearance of symptoms of infestation.

cauliflower/insect.2.name: Whitefly
cauliflower/insect.2.symptom: The nymphs and adults feed on the lower surface of cauliflower leaves, and this feeding results in spots that appear on the upper surface of the leaf and turn yellow, and the leaves may curl in the case of virus infection.
cauliflower/insect.2.timing: As soon as individuals are detected on the lower surface of the leaf.

cauliflower/fungus.3.name: Sclerotinia white mould
cauliflower/fungus.3.symptom: Symptoms appear on any part of the plant, especially on the stem near the soil surface, and the infection is in the form of small watery spots that later turn brown; the infection may extend downward, infecting the root system, and also extends up the stem until it reaches the bases and petioles of the leaves, causing their yellowing and wilting. The spots on the stem and branches may turn into cankers and the growth of the white cottony fungus appears, and the infected tissues become soft, pink or brown in colour, covered with a white cottony rot, with the beginning of the appearance of masses of dense fungal growth distributed irregularly on the infected tissues, which are the beginnings of the formation of sclerotia, and finally these sclerotia take on a black colour and their length ranges between 2 mm - 1 cm or more and their shapes are irregular.
cauliflower/fungus.3.appearance: When suitable conditions are available, especially high relative humidity and low temperatures.

artichoke/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
artichoke/insect.1.symptom: Newly hatched larvae feed on the leaf epidermis around the egg-mass site and it widens until it covers the leaf surface and the leaf appears thin and transparent, then dries, and holes also occur in it, in addition to the buds, flowers and the small fruit set, and the larva makes tunnels inside the fruits and the tunnel opening is irregular.
artichoke/insect.1.appearance: From the beginning of seedling emergence until the end of the season.
artichoke/insect.1.timing: When signs of larval feeding are seen or an infestation rate of 5 % is present.

lettuce/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
lettuce/insect.1.symptom: Newly hatched larvae feed on the surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe with the presence of older larvae, they feed on the entire leaves from the heart to the outer leaves, causing damage to the plant's foliage.
lettuce/insect.1.appearance: From the emergence of seedlings until harvest.
lettuce/insect.1.timing: At the start of the appearance of symptoms of infestation.

spinach/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
spinach/insect.1.symptom: First-instar larvae feed on the surface of the leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe with the presence of larvae of older instars, they feed making holes in the leaves and cause their damage.
spinach/insect.1.timing: As soon as the first symptom of infestation appears.

strawberry/insect.1.name: Cotton leafworm
strawberry/insect.1.symptom: Newly hatched larvae feed on the lower epidermis of the leaves.
strawberry/insect.1.appearance: November and December - March and April.
strawberry/insect.1.guidance: Spraying is done on the foliage.

strawberry/mite.2.name: Red spider mite
strawberry/mite.2.symptom: Yellow spots appear on the leaves - roughness of the leaf surface in the areas where individuals are present - yellowing of the leaf surface and its wilting.
strawberry/mite.2.appearance: In two periods: the first late October and early November; the second mid-March and during April.
strawberry/mite.2.timing: When the average number of mites reaches 5 moving individuals on the leaf surface in leaves examined at random.
strawberry/mite.2.guidance: Spraying is done on the foliage.

strawberry/fungus.3.name: Fruit rots
strawberry/fungus.3.symptom: It is caused by numerous fungi, some of which cause soft rot, dry rot, leathery rot and grey mould on the fruits.
strawberry/fungus.3.appearance: From the beginning of fruit set and in the different stages of fruit growth.
strawberry/fungus.3.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

strawberry/fungus.4.name: Powdery mildew
strawberry/fungus.4.symptom: Symptoms appear in the form of upward curling of the leaves so that they take the shape of a spoon and often tend to purple colour, and the lower surface of the leaves has a powdery white growth which then spreads to the upper surface, and in case of severe infection the flowers and their stalks are infected, with the white growth appearing on them, or the white growths may appear on the fruits at different stages of growth.
strawberry/fungus.4.appearance: The infection spreads in warm weather and high humidity.
strawberry/fungus.4.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

strawberry/fungus.5.name: Root rot disease
strawberry/fungus.5.symptom: Brown cankers occur on the roots, then they become black in colour; as a result the feeding root hairs die and the blackening spreads until it covers the whole root system, whose cortex rots and separates from the vascular cylinder, which leads to yellowing of the plants and their wilting, and it becomes easy to pull the plants out of the soil.
strawberry/fungus.5.appearance: At the beginning of the plant's life and at any stage of plant growth.

strawberry/fungus.6.name: Leaf spot
strawberry/fungus.6.symptom: Purple spots with a grey centre and bluish-red margins. They appear on the leaves and their petioles and may reach the flower calyces, and round, oval or triangular spots also appear, reddish-brown in colour with violet margins.
strawberry/fungus.6.appearance: At any stage of plant growth.
strawberry/fungus.6.timing: At the start of the appearance of the symptoms.

protected/nematode.1.name: Soil nematodes (sterilants)
protected/nematode.1.symptom: Knots appear on the roots (in cucumber under protected cultivation or strawberry in open fields), followed by yellowing of the leaves, wilting and stunting of the plant.
protected/nematode.1.appearance: From the seedling stage to the fruiting plant.
protected/nematode.1.timing: The soil is sterilised about one month before planting when the root-knot index is at least 2 in the previous crop. Control is carried out when the knot index is less than 2 in the previous crop and when planting seedlings.
protected/nematode.1.guidance: The same treatments are used in the case of infestation by other types of nematodes such as the reniform nematode.

protected/nematode.2.name: Soil nematodes (control)
protected/nematode.2.symptom: Slight infections appear on seedlings such as some cankers on the secondary roots, and slight yellowing also appears on the leaves and foliage.
protected/nematode.2.appearance: From the seedling stage to the fruiting plant.
protected/nematode.2.timing: When planting the seedling in the case of slight soil contamination (less than 2 root-knot index) or some other harmful nematode species.
protected/nematode.2.guidance: Control of harmful nematodes that infect plants is carried out in the case of slight soil contamination with root-knot nematode or some other species.

green_areas/insect.1.name: Pests of green areas (lawns)
green_areas/insect.1.symptom: - Yellowing of the plants, the yellowing being in the form of irregular patches. - When the infested grass is lifted, it separates from the soil and rises from the ground like a carpet
green_areas/insect.1.appearance: Larvae and adults of the hard-backed beetle are abundant in the soil from September until February and from March until August, feeding on the roots and causing the death of the plant.
green_areas/insect.1.timing: - When there is infestation on the lawn - chemical control is preferably carried out before planting the lawn - the control operation is carried out at the beginning of symptoms of infestation on the plants or when larvae are seen.
green_areas/insect.1.guidance: Care for agricultural operations and do not use fresh farmyard manure containing larvae of the pest.

green_areas/fungus.2.name: Leaf spot
green_areas/fungus.2.symptom: Damage appears on the leaves as dark circular elliptical rings that develop on the blade and stems; some spots become red, purple or brown with dark borders; the colour of the turf becomes yellowish brown with disease development and it becomes thin and the turf can die. There is also dollar spot disease, so named because of the presence of brown spots the size of a silver dollar in the ground, which soon develop, and the plants take on the colour of straw, and the spots can also be observed on the leaves.

citrus/insect.1.name: Scale insects
citrus/insect.1.symptom: Presence of nymphs, adults and egg sacs on the branches and leaves; the insects gather along the midribs, especially the lower surface - growth of the black mould fungus on the leaves and fruits - presence of ants feeding on the honeydew secretions that the insect secretes abundantly - yellowing of the leaves, wilting them in case of severe infestation, small size of the fruits formed and their deformation.
citrus/insect.1.appearance: It appears throughout the year and has 4 - 5 generations per year - it infests citrus, especially baladi lemon.
citrus/insect.1.timing: When infestation is present on 5% of the trees examined at random in the orchard.
citrus/insect.1.guidance: When spraying, care should be taken that the ground is irrigated - use a sound tilting motor - spraying in the early morning after the dew has evaporated. The instructions for using oils (Appendix Two) should be observed.

citrus/insect.2.name: Fruit flies
citrus/insect.2.symptom: Puncture marks appear on the body of the fruit with a change in the colour of the area surrounding the punctures and softness inside the fruit as a result of the transformation of the larvae; when pressed, liquid comes out of it, and fruit drop is observed around the tree.
citrus/insect.2.appearance: In the months of October and November.
citrus/insect.2.timing: When infestations appear on the fruits.
citrus/insect.2.guidance: The fallen fruits must be disposed of immediately by burying or burning. The instructions for lethal bundles (bait clusters) and partial spraying (Appendix Two) are to be observed.

citrus/insect.3.name: Leafminers
citrus/insect.3.symptom: Presence of mines on either surface of the leaf as a result of the larvae feeding between the two epidermises of the leaf; severe infestation leads to drying of the leaves, and tender newly grown stems may also be infested, with the mines appearing clearly on them.
citrus/insect.3.appearance: Infestation occurs all year round, and its presence is linked to the presence of tender new growth, and it is more abundant in the nursery than in evergreen (mature) trees.

citrus/mite.4.name: Citrus brown mite
citrus/mite.4.symptom: Appearance of yellow spots - on the upper surface of the leaves - which turn brown, dry and fall. The chlorophyll content decreases in green fruits as a result of sap sucking, and consequently the fruit appears pale in colour and smooth in texture. As for yellow fruits, brown spots appear on them as the infestation increases.
citrus/mite.4.appearance: The infestation begins in March and increases from July until the following February.
citrus/mite.4.timing: When 5 or more individuals are present on a leaf from the group of leaves examined at random.

citrus/mite.5.name: Citrus red mite
citrus/mite.5.symptom: - This species is found on the lower surface of the leaves and causes them to turn yellow, then moves on to the fruits and causes them to dry - cracks occur in the fruits and they turn dark brown - appearance of pale, sunken silvery spots (left).
citrus/mite.5.timing: At the beginning of the appearance of the infestation.
citrus/mite.5.guidance: Keeping the field clean of weeds, with getting rid of perennial plants such as hedges

citrus/mite.6.name: Citrus rust mite
citrus/mite.6.symptom: Rust-coloured spots appear on the lower surface of the leaves, starting from the edge of the leaf, and as the infestation increases they cover the lower surface of the leaf. On the fruits, small rust-coloured spots appear on one of their sides and begin to increase until they take a rusty form around the middle of the fruit, and in the case of severe infestation they take a rusty form covering the whole fruit, and in the case of lemon a silvery colour appears on the leaves and fruits.
citrus/mite.6.appearance: The infestation begins in mid-May and increases in July and August and decreases in October. The infestation may appear very early, starting from January.
citrus/mite.6.timing: When 5 individuals are present on the leaf or fruit from the group of leaves or fruits examined at random.
citrus/mite.6.guidance: Spraying when the infestation appears and repeating the spraying when needed, and the spraying should be uniform

citrus/other.7.name: Lichens
citrus/other.7.symptom: Scaly growths of different colours (or shell-like, tending towards greenish yellow) on branches and new growth, increasing with increased humidity.
citrus/other.7.appearance: At any time of the year.
citrus/other.7.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.
citrus/other.7.guidance: The plants are sprayed as soon as the infestation appears, and spraying is stopped a sufficient period before harvest.

citrus/other.8.name: Gummosis
citrus/other.8.symptom: Presence of gummy spots on the tree trunk, brown in colour, with a distinctive smell.
citrus/other.8.appearance: At any time of the year.
citrus/other.8.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.

citrus/fungus.9.name: Post-harvest fruit rots
citrus/fungus.9.symptom: The infection appears in the form of black spots on the surface of the fruit, especially the end of the fruit; it can also appear in the form of soft, watery (tender) spots on the fruit peel at the site of infection, then these spots are quickly covered and a white fungal growth appears on their surface, followed by the appearance of an olive-green, greyish-blue or brown colour, which consists of the spores of the fungi that cause the rot.
citrus/fungus.9.appearance: This disease appears in the field at the stage of maturity of the citrus fruit, and it also appears after harvest in the store in the case of poor storage conditions.
citrus/fungus.9.timing: When the infection begins to appear in the field or after picking and sorting before storage.

citrus/nematode.10.name: Slow decline nematode (in fruit-bearing trees)
citrus/nematode.10.symptom: Death of terminal branches - lesions on the root system - ease of separating the bark region of the roots from the vascular bundle - soil particles sticking to the secondary feeder roots.
citrus/nematode.10.appearance: Symptoms do not appear on citrus trees until several years after their infestation, in the form of dieback of the tips and drying of the upper branches.
citrus/nematode.10.timing: When 4000 individuals are present in 250 g of soil at the beginning of the season (February and March).

citrus/nematode.11.name: Slow decline nematode (in new plantings)
citrus/nematode.11.symptom: Death of terminal branches - lesions on the root system - ease of separating the bark region of the roots from the vascular bundle - soil particles sticking to the secondary feeder roots.
citrus/nematode.11.appearance: Symptoms appear on a limited number of citrus trees, then spread and include most of the trees after several years.
citrus/nematode.11.timing: When 2400 individuals are present in 250 g of soil at the beginning of the season.

citrus/fungus.12.name: Navel-end rot
citrus/fungus.12.symptom: Blackening in the navel area, and when the fruit is cut lengthwise the extension of the black colour is seen.
citrus/fungus.12.timing: Preventive spraying starting from the first of May.

mango/insect.1.name: Mealybugs
mango/insect.1.symptom: Presence of insects covered with white waxy secretions - growth of black fungus - presence of ants that feed on the honeydew secretion of the insects.
mango/insect.1.appearance: Infestation all year round, and it decreases in winter, when the intermediate adult stages disappear in the cracks in the lower parts of the tree.
mango/insect.1.timing: When about 5 % of the number of trees are infested, taking into account the percentage of infested leaves on a single tree.
mango/insect.1.guidance: The precautions for spraying oils (Appendix Two) should be observed

mango/insect.2.name: Scale insects
mango/insect.2.symptom: Females and nymphs suck the sap from the leaf, leading to the appearance of yellow colour on the leaves - for soft scale insects the appearance of the infestation is accompanied by black mould fungus that grows on the honeydew secreted by the insects.
mango/insect.2.appearance: The infestation is present all year round and becomes severe from June until August.
mango/insect.2.timing: When the infestation reaches 10 % of the leaves on a single tree and when 10 % of the trees in the orchard are infested, from the group of leaves or trees examined at random.
mango/insect.2.guidance: The precautions for spraying oils (Appendix Two) should be observed

mango/insect.3.name: Fruit flies
mango/insect.3.symptom: Puncture marks appear on the body of the fruit with a gummy liquid in fruits that are not fully ripe, and softness in the area of the puncture and the sap comes out when pressed.
mango/insect.3.appearance: In the months of July and August
mango/insect.3.guidance: The fallen fruits must be disposed of immediately by burying or burning. The instructions for lethal bundles (bait clusters) and partial spraying (Appendix Two) are to be observed.

mango/fungus.4.name: Powdery mildew
mango/fungus.4.symptom: A white powdery coating on young leaves, flower stalks and small fruits, leading to the death of the infected tissues and their turning brown.
mango/fungus.4.appearance: Since the emergence of the new leaves and flower stalks.

mango/fungus.5.name: Flower blight (anthracnose)
mango/fungus.5.symptom: Wilting of the flower stalks and death of the infected flowers and their turning brown and then black.
mango/fungus.5.timing: When the beginning of the infection appears.

mango/fungus.6.name: Sooty mould
mango/fungus.6.symptom: It appears in the form of a black layer covering the leaves and fruits as a result of infestation by piercing-sucking insects and not controlling them properly at the right time, but it does not appear suddenly; rather it appears gradually with the progress of the insect infestation by piercing-sucking insects such as aphids, thrips, scale insects and mealybugs.
mango/fungus.6.appearance: This disease appears on mango trees at any time of the year, especially in neglected farms with excessive use of nitrogen fertilisers that make the leaves tender and more prone to insect infestations, and increased irrigation rates, which increase the humidity level with which the fungi causing black sooty mould disease become active.
mango/fungus.6.timing: When the beginning of the infection appears.

grape/insect.1.name: Mealybugs
grape/insect.1.symptom: Appearance of white-coloured insects on the leaves and bark. Then the bark becomes loose and is peeled off easily, with individuals present under the bark, then infestation by black mould appears, which grows on the honeydew and covers the stems with black colour.
grape/insect.1.appearance: They are present in winter hidden under the bark in the lower trunk area. In spring the individuals appear on the stems and move to the bunches in summer.
grape/insect.1.guidance: After pruning the tree it is advised to peel off the bark and burn the pruning residues. When spraying, the high-volume (mist) spray is to be in an umbrella form, taking care not to spray during flowering and fruit set.

grape/insect.2.name: Fruit flies
grape/insect.2.symptom: - Presence of dark-coloured scars on the surface of the fruit from which a gummy secretion comes out, and the puncture area turns into a soft, fermented area, causing rot and fruit drop. - It infests fruits near ripening, where it damages the fruits and leads to their rotting.
grape/insect.2.timing: When the infestation begins to appear
grape/insect.2.guidance: - Early picking of the fruits to prevent infestation, and collecting the fallen infested fruits and destroying them.

grape/insect.3.name: Thrips
grape/insect.3.symptom: Silvery spots appear on the leaf as a result of the insect feeding on the plant sap, and the adult insects appear in their black colour and the nymphs in yellow, with a maximum ranging from 7 - 10 insects per plant.
grape/insect.3.appearance: Starting from April until the end of the season, but their numbers begin to increase gradually from late May until the crop ripens.

grape/insect.4.name: Grape berry moth (grape fruit worm)
grape/insect.4.symptom: The larva makes a set of silken threads with which it ties the grape fruits at all stages of growth (flower buds - fruits not fully ripe - fully ripe fruits) and thus makes a mass of fruits from inside which the larva feeds.
grape/insect.4.appearance: Starting from April until July, and it has three generations. A first generation on the flower buds, the second generation on fruits not fully ripe, and the third generation, which is the most dangerous of them, on fully ripe fruits.
grape/insect.4.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.

grape/mite.5.name: Red spider mite
grape/mite.5.symptom: Presence of yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves, and as the infestation progresses they turn brown, then the leaves dry and fall.
grape/mite.5.appearance: With the beginning of the appearance of the leaves in March, April, and the infestation increases gradually until August and September.
grape/mite.5.timing: When 5 individuals are present on the lower surface of the leaves from the group of leaves examined at random.
grape/mite.5.guidance: The plants are sprayed with the pesticide preparation, covering the lower surface of the leaves.

grape/fungus.6.name: Fruit rots
grape/fungus.6.symptom: Growth of the berries stops and their skin cracks - appearance of growths of different colours depending on the causal agent - disintegration of the berry skin and the internal juice coming out with a change in its colour.
grape/fungus.6.appearance: From the first of June to the end of the season.
grape/fungus.6.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.

grape/fungus.7.name: Powdery mildew
grape/fungus.7.symptom: A white powdery coating on all infected parts (leaves - flowers - fruits).
grape/fungus.7.appearance: When the leaves and flowers emerge and the fruits set.
grape/fungus.7.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.
grape/fungus.7.guidance: Spraying starts when the new growth reaches about 30 cm and is repeated according to the severity of the infection.

grape/fungus.8.name: Downy mildew
grape/fungus.8.symptom: Yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves and the appearance of a downy growth on the lower surface.
grape/fungus.8.appearance: From the second half of May to the end of the season.
grape/fungus.8.timing: When the symptoms begin to appear.

grape/nematode.9.name: Root-knot nematode
grape/nematode.9.symptom: Galls on the roots - yellowing of the foliage.
grape/nematode.9.appearance: From the seedling stage until the end of the season.
grape/nematode.9.timing: Any numbers in the soil at the beginning of the season are considered dangerous and deserve treatment.
grape/nematode.9.guidance: Grapes are infested by the citrus nematode, and the same treatments are also used for control.

dates/insect.1.name: Red palm weevil
dates/insect.1.symptom: A brown, sticky-textured, foul-smelling liquid comes out of holes on the tree trunks - as the infestation progresses, cavities and tunnels appear inside the tree trunks containing all stages of the insect - drying of the growing tip of offshoots and trees - falling of the palm's crown - drying of the outer leaves of the palm.
dates/insect.1.guidance: The recommended pesticide solution is injected inside a hole made with a long nail with a diameter of 1.5 cm at the focus of infestation and around it in a circular pattern at a depth ranging between 10-15 cm. Injection continues until the pesticide flows back out of the hole, then injection is followed up after 5-7 days. Each infestation site is treated separately.

dates/mite.2.name: Date palm dust mite
dates/mite.2.symptom: Appearance of spots on the upper leaves, and when the infestation becomes severe, spider-like webs form on the lower surface of the leaves and on the fruits.
dates/mite.2.appearance: The mites begin to appear on the fruits starting from the end of March until the end of October, and varieties differ in their sensitivity to infestation, as some varieties show infestation early and other varieties show infestation late.
dates/mite.2.timing: Control of the date palm dust mite by traditional methods, the most important of which is washing the infested fruit stalks with water under pressure, in the areas where infestation appears several weeks after fruit set and periodically, and the recommended pesticides are also sprayed on the date palm dust mite during the season to get rid of the mite; taking care of irrigation and not letting the trees go thirsty and getting rid of weeds under and around the trees; some also resort to cutting off the infested fruit stalks and getting rid of them by burning them away from the farm.

sykes_palm/insect.1.name: Abu Daqiq of the Sykes palm
sykes_palm/insect.1.symptom: They eat the heart of the palm, especially the tender buds, and cause them to dry, and the pupal skins of the moths appear.
sykes_palm/insect.1.appearance: All year round because of the presence of nearly 12 generations of moths during the year.
sykes_palm/insect.1.timing: As soon as the symptoms of infestation appear.

olive/insect.1.name: Scale insects
olive/insect.1.symptom: Different ages are present on the trunks - branches - leaves - fruits - they cause drying of the leaves and their fall as they suck the plant sap - infestation by the olive scale insect causes death of the terminal branches, then the main branches, then death of the tree - they cause red spots on the fruits at the site of infestation by the olive scale insect - as for the soft olive insect, it secretes honeydew.
olive/insect.1.appearance: Different stages of the insects are present on infested trees all year round - for the soft olive insect the most active periods are August and September - as for the olive oystershell and scale insects, they have three generations per year.
olive/insect.1.guidance: The precautions for spraying oils (Appendix Two) should be observed

olive/insect.2.name: Olive leafworm
olive/insect.2.symptom: - The larvae feed on the leaves, buds, flowers and fruits - damage to new growth and flower buds and their falling before fruit set
olive/insect.2.timing: Starting from May with repeated spraying monthly.
olive/insect.2.guidance: Getting rid of weeds and fallen leaves to prevent the larvae from pupating in them.

olive/fungus.3.name: Leaf spot
olive/fungus.3.symptom: Dark brown spots on the leaves surrounded by a yellow halo, resembling a bird's eye.
olive/fungus.3.appearance: From the second half of August.

guava/insect.1.name: Soft scale insect (Pulvinaria)
guava/insect.1.symptom: Presence of adult insects and nymphs on the leaves, branches and fruits - growth of black mould fungus - presence of ants that feed on the honeydew secreted by these insects.
guava/insect.1.appearance: Adult insects and nymphs appear all year round, with the winter period spent in the form of egg sacs or adult insects in the cracks and lower parts of the trees and the inner branches.
guava/insect.1.timing: When the infestation reaches about 5 % of all trees examined at random, taking into account the infestation rate on a single tree.
guava/insect.1.guidance: Washing the trees well with the high-volume (mist) spray liquid, without spraying in hot weather, and spraying is preferably done in the spring period when the largest proportion of the population of immature stages is present. The precautions for spraying oils (Appendix Two) should be observed.

guava/insect.2.name: Aphids
guava/insect.2.symptom: The aphid sucks the plant sap through its piercing-sucking mouthparts and secretes honeydew on which black mould fungi grow, affecting photosynthesis, and the infestation leads to curling and deformation of the leaves, especially the terminal growth.
guava/insect.2.timing: Spraying begins when the leaf infestation rate reaches 5-6 % of all trees examined at random.

guava/mite.3.name: Guava leaf rust mite
guava/mite.3.symptom: Appearance of silvery leaves that reach a bronze colour in the advanced stage of infestation, starting mild then covering the entire leaf, and it may lead to leaf drop in the case of infestation of young trees.
guava/mite.3.appearance: In the case of the appearance of new leaves and the appearance of buds.
guava/mite.3.timing: As soon as 3-4 individuals appear on the leaf.

guava/mite.4.name: Flat mite on guava fruits
guava/mite.4.symptom: It attacks the fruits, and when the infestation becomes severe the skin of the fruits becomes rough and turns grey, and superficial cracks appear on it among which the mite lives to lay eggs in them.
guava/mite.4.timing: As soon as the infestation appears, starting from March until May, at a rate of 5 individuals per fruit.

guava/fungus.5.name: Leaf spot
guava/fungus.5.symptom: This disease results from infection by the fungus Cercospora psidii or Cercospora sawadae, and the symptoms are the appearance of white spots on the leaves, round or irregular, forming a reddish-brown or brown colour, and old leaves are usually infected, and when the infection is severe these leaves curl and fall.
guava/fungus.5.appearance: The disease increases from December to February

pomegranate/insect.1.name: Aphids
pomegranate/insect.1.symptom: The aphid sucks the plant sap through its piercing-sucking mouthparts and secretes honeydew on which black mould fungi grow, affecting photosynthesis, and the infestation leads to curling and deformation of the leaves, especially the terminal growth.
pomegranate/insect.1.timing: When the tree infestation rate reaches 5 % of all trees examined at random.

pomegranate/insect.2.name: Mealybugs
pomegranate/insect.2.symptom: The insects are present on the lower surface of the leaves and suck the plant sap and secrete honeydew at the beginning of the season, and after the bunches form the insects move to the fruits and begin to suck the sap, and contamination of the grape bunches by cottony egg sacs, larvae, adult insects and honeydew is observed, and black sooty mould usually appears on the honeydew if suitable weather conditions are available, and the insects hide under the bark and around the roots at the end of the season, where they spend the winter.
pomegranate/insect.2.timing: As soon as symptoms of infestation appear or individuals appear on the lower surface of the leaves.

pomegranate/insect.3.name: Pomegranate butterfly (Abu Daqiq)
pomegranate/insect.3.symptom: The larvae attack and damage its contents, and the symptoms of a black ring appear around the site of the infested hole, so rot of the fruits occurs as a result of feeding on the contents of the fruit.
pomegranate/insect.3.appearance: The adult insects appear in early spring during the flowering period and at the beginning of fruit set.

apple/insect.1.name: Apple stem borer
apple/insect.1.symptom: Appearance of pupal skins on the trees and falling of wood shavings and feeding products around the tree trunk.
apple/insect.1.timing: During the months from March until June.
apple/insect.1.guidance: Care should be taken to wash the trees well (the trunk area and large branches) with the pesticide solution.

apple/insect.2.name: Woolly apple aphid
apple/insect.2.symptom: The nymphs and adult insects feed by sucking plant sap from the stems, branches and roots, which results in the appearance of swellings, cankers and deformities in the feeding areas, causing drying of the infested branches and death of parts of them; swellings accumulate on top of each other, and white fluff appears between the folds of these swellings covering the different stages, and these swellings also occur on the roots; honeydew forms and black mould fungus grows, and growth is delayed and it causes death of the trees.
apple/insect.2.appearance: During the spring and summer seasons, and the infestation becomes severe in the months of July and August.
apple/insect.2.timing: At the time of flowering during the month of April.

apple/mite.3.name: European red mite (overwintering eggs)
apple/mite.3.symptom: Red colour on the branches and spurs and in the axils of the buds due to the presence of clusters of dark red eggs.
apple/mite.3.timing: When 10 eggs are present on a spur with a terminal bud.

apple/mite.4.name: European red mite (mobile stages)
apple/mite.4.symptom: Hatching begins and the red-coloured larvae emerge in late February and early March, which attack the flower buds and damage them, and it may even reach the point of destroying them; these larvae turn into the first and second nymphs and then the adult stages, and mating takes place between the female and the male to lay fertilised eggs that give males and females that attack the new leaves severely; this species is found on the upper surface of the leaves and, in the case of severe infestation, on both the lower and upper surfaces; individuals gradually increase until they reach their peak in September
apple/mite.4.appearance: The eggs remain present on the branches until late February and early March, and hatching begins and the red-coloured larvae emerge, which attack the flower buds and damage them in the same preceding period.
apple/mite.4.timing: Control operations begin starting from January until March

apple/mite.5.name: Red spider mite
apple/mite.5.symptom: Pale yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves and around the midribs, and as the infestation progresses general yellowing of the leaves, drying and falling occur.
apple/mite.5.appearance: According to the environmental conditions in the area of cultivation - during March, April, May.
apple/mite.5.timing: When 5 or more individuals are present on a leaf from the group of leaves examined at random.
apple/mite.5.guidance: Care should be taken that the treated surface is fully covered by the spraying methods.

apple/fungus.6.name: Powdery mildew
apple/fungus.6.symptom: White powdery spots on all above-ground parts of the plant (leaves - flowers).
apple/fungus.6.appearance: When the vegetative growth and flowers appear.
apple/fungus.6.timing: At the start of the appearance of the infection.

apple/fungus.7.name: Scab
apple/fungus.7.symptom: Leathery spots on the leaves that turn brown, with the appearance of areas of different colour, rough in texture and appearance, on the fruits.
apple/fungus.7.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.

pear/insect.1.name: Scale insect
pear/insect.1.symptom: Grey layers of insect scales on the branches - these layers can be removed by hand, with a sticky red liquid appearing from the bodies of the live insects - death of the branches and their turning brown - red spots on the fruits.
pear/insect.1.appearance: The insects are present all year round in the form of dense layers on the branches and some fruits - the infestation becomes severe in March and April and then August and September.
pear/insect.1.timing: It is advised to start spraying when the tree infestation rate reaches 5 - 6 % of all trees examined at random.
pear/insect.1.guidance: Spraying in April and September, covering all areas of the infestation foci, taking into account the instructions for controlling pests of citrus and orchards.

pear/fungus.2.name: Lichens
pear/fungus.2.symptom: Scaly growths of different colours (or shell-like, tending towards greenish yellow) on branches and new growth - increasing with increased humidity.
pear/fungus.2.appearance: At any time of the year.
pear/fungus.2.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.

pear/bacterium.3.name: Fire blight
pear/bacterium.3.symptom: The infection occurs through the flower stigmas, where the colour of the flowers and leaves on the spur turns black, with bacterial exudates on the flower and leaf stalks, in the case of high atmospheric humidity of 80 % or more with rainfall. The infection extends to the base of the spur and then to the branches bearing the spurs in the form of cankers, which extend to the branches and tree trunks in severe infections.
pear/bacterium.3.appearance: The infection appears in spring, especially in the second week of April - where the atmospheric conditions are suitable for the multiplication and spread of the bacterial inoculum - after the flowers open, when they wilt and turn black.
pear/bacterium.3.timing: The appearance of the first infection spot in the field is considered the deciding factor for applying the treatment programme.

peach/insect.1.name: Fruit flies
peach/insect.1.symptom: Puncture marks appear on the body of the fruit and softness at the site of the puncture with sap coming out when pressed.
peach/insect.1.timing: When symptoms of infestation are noticed.

peach/mite.2.name: Red spider mite
peach/mite.2.symptom: Pale yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaves and around the midribs, and as the infestation progresses general yellowing of the leaves, drying and falling occur.
peach/mite.2.appearance: According to the environmental conditions in the area of cultivation - during March, April, May.
peach/mite.2.timing: When 5 or more individuals are present on the leaf.
peach/mite.2.guidance: Care should be taken that the treated surface is fully covered by the solution.

peach/fungus.3.name: Powdery mildew
peach/fungus.3.symptom: White powdery growths on all above-ground parts of the plant (leaves - flowers).
peach/fungus.3.appearance: At the start of the emergence of vegetative growth and flowers and fruit set.
peach/fungus.3.timing: At the start of the appearance of symptoms of infestation.

peach/fungus.4.name: Brown rot
peach/fungus.4.symptom: Soft brown spots appear on the fruits and grow larger as the fruit progresses in ripening, and the inner heart of the fruit rots and then it falls to the ground; infection may occur on the farm but remains latent and appears only at the time of picking or before picking when the fruits are green; the fruits may remain hanging on the trees but lose their water content completely, and rot fungi then grow saprophytically on them.
peach/fungus.4.appearance: During flowering or before picking and at picking time.
peach/fungus.4.timing: At the beginning of the infection of the flowers and fruits.

peach/fungus.5.name: Peach rust
peach/fungus.5.symptom: Symptoms appear in the form of yellow spots on the upper surface of the leaf, corresponding on the lower surface to an orange colour consisting of accumulations of the fungus spores, which turn dark brown as the infection develops.
peach/fungus.5.appearance: During the period from March to April.

peach/fungus.6.name: Peach leaf curl
peach/fungus.6.symptom: Appearance of scattered dark-coloured, leathery-looking areas, thicker than the rest of the areas, on the leaves, and the leaf becomes wavy.
peach/fungus.6.timing: At the start of the appearance of symptoms of infestation.

apricot/fungus.1.name: Powdery mildew
apricot/fungus.1.symptom: A white powdery-looking coating on all above-ground parts of the plant, leading to death and browning of the infected tissues.
apricot/fungus.1.appearance: When the new growth, flowers and fruits emerge.
apricot/fungus.1.timing: When the infestation begins to appear.

banana/nematode.1.name: Root-knot nematode
banana/nematode.1.symptom: Galls on the roots - yellowing of the leaves - stunting of the plants - reduced yield - it may be accompanied by rots on the root system.
banana/nematode.1.appearance: Throughout the growing season, especially at the beginning of the root growing season.
banana/nematode.1.timing: When any numbers of root-knot nematode larvae are present in the soil at the beginning of the season.
banana/nematode.1.guidance: It is preferable to add nematicides when there is no crop on the trees. Banana is also infested by some harmful types of nematodes such as spiral nematodes and citrus nematodes, so it is recommended to use the same treatments and recommendations. The quantity of pesticide is placed in the planting hole twice, the first in May and the other after four months, and then the land is irrigated immediately after treatment.

stored_crops/insect.1.name: Stored grain insects
stored_crops/insect.1.symptom: Presence of adult stages of moths and beetles in the storage places - presence of perforated or eroded grains - presence of a powdery coating on the surface of the sacks - presence of insect droppings in the grains - appearance of a foul smell - rise in the temperature of the stored grain and in the carbon dioxide level.
stored_crops/insect.1.timing: At the beginning of storage (Appendix Three).
stored_crops/insect.1.guidance: Treatment is carried out at the beginning of storage to prevent infestation and is handled only by specialists.

stored_crops/insect.2.name: Stored date insects
stored_crops/insect.2.symptom: The moth lays eggs on the fruits while they are still on the palms, and also on fallen and stored dates, and on the fruits during drying, and the eggs hatch into larvae that feed on the date, leaving behind their droppings and a network of silken threads. As for date beetles, the larvae feed in the area confined between the fruit skin and its flesh, forming in this area a natural void that grows wider the more the insect's activity increases, and the larvae's droppings are observed in the same area.
stored_crops/insect.2.appearance: From the beginning of September until mid-October.

buildings/insect.1.name: Termites
buildings/insect.1.symptom: Presence of mud tunnels on the walls - presence of erosion in wood or cellulosic materials - and when the wood breaks, the tunnels and the insects inside them appear.
buildings/insect.1.guidance: The pesticide is made to reach the insects' tunnels by injection and by pouring the solution into trenches made around the walls of the buildings with a depth of 30 cm and a width of 30 cm until saturation, and the infested area is injected at a rate of 4 L / hole at 1 m intervals.

open_fields/other.1.name: Rats and mice
open_fields/other.1.symptom: In agricultural fields, rodents feed on grains and seeds when they are planted, and also on seedlings and then fruits. In fruit orchards, rodents feed on young buds, gnaw the bark of trees and feed on the fruits.
open_fields/other.1.timing: From the beginning of planting to harvest.
open_fields/other.1.guidance: Anticoagulant (blood-thinning) pesticides are used from the start of planting, weekly, until consumption of the poisoned bait used stops.

snails/mollusc.1.name: Snails
snails/mollusc.1.symptom: Snails attack all plant parts, especially the tender parts, and cause great damage to them, and they also stick to the trunks and stems of plants and trees during the summer season, and the population may reach the point of covering these plant parts, which affects their vitality. In the case of infestation of fruit, they stick to it and cause deformities of the fruit and thus a bad effect on its marketing quality.
snails/mollusc.1.appearance: Land snails are nocturnal animals, and the longest season of their activity - as a pest - is the spring season followed by autumn and winter, and the activity of snails increases where soil moisture rises and temperature becomes moderate, whereas during the summer months most snails stick to supports, plant stems, branches and palms, where they enter a resting phase and stop moving and feeding, and they close the opening of the shell with a membrane that protects the snail's body from moisture loss.
snails/mollusc.1.timing: The chemical control programme using poisoned bait is applied during the periods of snail activity, especially during the period from February until May.
snails/mollusc.1.guidance: To the quantity required per feddan are added 5 kg of bran and half a kg of molasses, mixed with about 2.5 L of water to make the poisoned bait. The bait is added by the handful between the plants or around tree trunks over moist soil.

wheat/insect.1.name: Pucerons
wheat/insect.1.symptom: Présence d'insectes regroupés sur les feuilles ; à mesure que l'infestation progresse, les effectifs augmentent et ils sécrètent un miellat sur lequel se développe le champignon de la fumagine noire.
wheat/insect.1.appearance: Pendant janvier et février ; l'infestation s'intensifie en mars.
wheat/insect.1.timing: Dès l'apparition d'infestations de pucerons, quel qu'en soit le nombre.
wheat/insect.1.guidance: Ne pas retarder la date de semis, vu la présence d'autres hôtes à partir desquels le ravageur passe aux mouches du blé.

wheat/fungus.2.name: Charbon nu du blé
wheat/fungus.2.symptom: Apparaît sur toutes les parties de l'épi sauf le rachis et les transforme en une masse pulvérulente noire de spores fongiques sombres. Les épis infectés sortent généralement quelques jours avant les épis sains. L'infection se propage par le vent, qui transporte les spores du champignon qui attaquent les épis sains au stade de la floraison. Le rachis des épis infectés apparaît complètement nu, sans aucun épillet, en fin de saison.
wheat/fungus.2.appearance: À l'épiaison, les épis infectés sortant précocement.
wheat/fungus.2.timing: Traitement des semences avant le semis :

wheat/fungus.3.name: Oïdium du blé
wheat/fungus.3.symptom: L'infection apparaît sur les feuilles sous forme de taches pâles gris-blanc, puis l'aspect poudreux caractéristique de cette maladie se forme sur la face supérieure des feuilles, avant de passer à la face inférieure à mesure que l'infection progresse. Lorsque l'infection devient sévère, de petits corps noirs apparaissent, qui sont les fructifications du champignon.
wheat/fungus.3.timing: Au début de l'apparition de l'infection.

wheat/fungus.4.name: Rouille jaune (striée)
wheat/fungus.4.symptom: Apparition de pustules légèrement saillantes à la surface de la feuille, de couleur jaune, de forme circulaire, disposées en rangées longitudinales parallèles à l'axe de la feuille, d'où le nom de rouille striée. Les pustules apparaissent sur toutes les parties de la plante (feuilles - tiges - gaines foliaires - épis). Lorsqu'on frotte à la main la feuille infectée, elle laisse des traces sous forme d'une poudre jaune.
wheat/fungus.4.appearance: Lorsque les conditions environnementales appropriées sont réunies, au début de la seconde quinzaine de février, les symptômes de la maladie commencent à apparaître sur les variétés sensibles, et la maladie se développe et se manifeste pendant mars et avril.

wheat/fungus.5.name: Maladies fusariennes du blé
wheat/fungus.5.symptom: C'est l'une des maladies secondaires qui ont été observées dans certains types de sols hors de la vallée (terres récupérées) ou dans des terres qui souffrent dans une certaine mesure de sécheresse. Les symptômes apparaissent sous forme d'une coloration brune du système racinaire et de la zone du collet, qui devient noire lorsque l'infection s'aggrave. L'infection des plantules entraîne leur mort, et l'infection de la plante adulte provoque le dessèchement des épis avant l'achèvement de la nouaison.
wheat/fungus.5.appearance: Cette maladie apparaît au stade plantule et au stade plante adulte.
wheat/fungus.5.timing: Traitement des semences avant le semis.

wheat/fungus.6.name: Pourriture des racines et fonte des semis
wheat/fungus.6.symptom: Il infecte les graines avant l'émergence de la plantule au-dessus de la surface du sol ; la radicule de l'embryon de la plante est atteinte de pourriture dès sa sortie de la graine, et dans ce cas les plantules n'apparaissent pas au-dessus de la surface du sol. Les plantules au-dessus de la surface du sol sont infectées, car le champignon attaque les plantules au niveau du sol ou légèrement en dessous, provoquant la pourriture de la tige, qui ne peut alors plus supporter les parties situées au-dessus d'elle.
wheat/fungus.6.appearance: Le champignon provoque la mort des plantes avant leur apparition au-dessus de la surface du sol, ou elles meurent dès qu'elles apparaissent au-dessus de la surface du sol.
wheat/fungus.6.timing: Traitement des semences avant le semis.

fieldbean/insect.1.name: Pucerons
